This supersedes the Supreme Cleave prestige class feature of the Knight Protector and Frenzied BerserkerCW.If your BAB is +16 or higher, you can activate this ability even if one of your allies (rather than you) drops an opponent that (a) is actively be in combat against you and your allies, (b) presents a credible threat (see above), and (c) is within your reach. This supersedes the prey on the weak stanceToB.
Synergy: If you also have the Staredown feat, if you make an additional attack thanks to Cleave and drop your target with that attack, all enemies witnessing the event are affected as if by your Staredown feat. This is an extraordinary [mind-affecting fear] effect that does not require an action on your part. This supersedes the Terrifying Warrior featDr343.
Note: The Pathfinder version of Cleave has been merged with Whirlwind Attack into the Whirlwind Strike feat (q.v.).

sections.heading: Combat AwarenessPHII
sections.text:
You have an uncanny ability to sense the ebb and flow of your opponents’ vitality.
Prerequisite: Wis 13, base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: During melee combat, you automatically know whether each adjacent creature is fatigued or exhausted. During non-combat situations, gaining this knowledge requires a standard action. This ability scales with your base attack bonus:
BAB +4: This ability extends to every creature you can see, not merely those adjacent to you.BAB +8: You automatically know if an unmoving creature you see is comatose, dying, actually dead, or merely faking it.BAB +12: You know the exact hp total of every adjacent creature.BAB +16: You know the exact hit point total of every creature you can see.

sections.heading: Critical, Dodge
sections.text:
You can turn even the luckiest blow into a grazing strike.
Prerequisites: Uncanny Dodge.
Benefit: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC for purposes of confirming critical hits against you. This bonus increases by +1 per 4 points of your base attack bonus.
In addition, you can attempt a Reflex saving throw to turn a critical hit against you into a normal hit. The save DC is equal to 10 + the attacker’s BAB + attacker’s Strength bonus (for melee attacks) or Wisdom bonus (for ranged attacks). The bonus you receive from this feat applies as a circumstance bonus to this save. You must be aware of the attack and not flat-footed, and you must declare the attempt before damage is rolled.
Source: This feat supersedes the Darkwood Stalker prestige class feature of the same nameCW, and also subsumes the Deny the Lethal Strike featRRE.

sections.heading: Crowd Control
sections.text:
You are skilled at making multiple assailants interfere with each other’s attacks.
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1, Alertness.
Benefit: As long as you have at least one immediate action available to you in a round, when threatened by more than one opponent you gain a circumstance bonus to AC equal to the total number of opponents threatening you. This bonus also applies to melee attack rolls you make against those opponents. The effects of this feat do not apply when you are flat-footed or otherwise denied your Dexterity bonus to AC. This ability scales with your base attack bonus, as follows:
BAB +4: Whenever you damage an opponent with a melee attack, until the start of your next turn, that opponent does not gain any circumstance bonus on attack rolls against you from Aid Another (for example, while it is flanking you) and cannot deal sneak attack damage to you. It can still provide Aid Another bonuses for its allies.BAB +8: Any opponent you damage in melee gains no Aid Another bonuses or flanking, and cannot provide them to others, until the end of your next turn. BAB +12: Opponents adjacent to you do not provide Aid Another bonuses or flanking to their allies.BAB +16: Opponents adjacent to you cannot provide or benefit from circumstance bonuses of any kind. BAB +20: The effects apply to all opponents within reach, not merely those adjacent to you.
Source: This feat subsumes the Urban Barbarian’s variant class feature of the same name, and also the Flanking Foil feat and the Flowing Monk’s “flowing dodge” variant class featuresUC. It also supersedes the chaotic good paladin’s Stand Against the Tide variant class featureBHM, the swarm tactics stanceToB, and the “cornered predator” option of the Reaping Talons featToB.

sections.heading: Defensive Combat Training
sections.text:
You have been trained to defend yourself from a variety of combat maneuvers.
Benefit: You treat your total Hit Dice as your base attack bonus when calculating your Combat Maneuver Defense. If your BAB is already equal to your Hit Dice, you instead gain a +4 competence bonus to CMD.

sections.heading: Defensive RebukeToB
sections.text:
You are better able to defend your allies against a designated enemy whose mettle you have tested.
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +6; Shared Shield feat or Challenge class feature.
Benefit: When you damage an opponent with a melee attack, you can select that opponent as the target of this feat. For the remainder of the encounter, any time that enemy attacks one of your allies (not you), he or she provokes an attack of opportunity from you by doing so. That opponent gains a passive Knowledge (warfare) check to identify this feat and its effects (Chapter 4).
If your base attack bonus is +11 or higher, you can designate additional targets of this feat after the first. Each such attempt is resolved as a [Strike] effect.If your base attack bonus is +16 or higher, all opponents you damage in melee are considered targets of this feat.

sections.heading: Dodge
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Dex 13.
Benefit: You gain a +1 dodge bonus to AC and CMD. Any condition that makes you lose your Dexterity bonus to AC also makes you lose the benefits of this feat.
If you are not wearing armor (or are wearing armor for which you have a –0 armor check penalty), and are not carrying a medium or heavy load, the dodge bonus increases by +1 for every four points of your base attack bonus (to a maximum of +6 at BAB +20).
Synergy: Certain classes can gain the benefits of this feat even if some of the normal conditions do not apply, as follows:
An unarmored barbarian can use a heavy shield and still gain the scaling dodge bonus. A monk applies the dodge bonus from this feat even when flat-footed.
Source: This feat now simulates the monk’s scaling bonus to AC, and also the Free Hand Fighter’s “elusive” variant class featureAPG.

sections.heading: Empowering Frustration
sections.text:
Benefit: During combat, for each round you miss on an attack roll or fail a combat maneuver check, or when a target successfully saves against a spell, spell-like ability, or supernatural ability you have cast or used, you gain a cumulative +1 morale bonus on attack rolls, damage rolls, saves, and checks. This bonus lasts until you successfully hit or perform a combat maneuver against a target, or until a target fails a saving throw against one of your spells, spell-like abilities, or supernatural abilities.
The maximum magnitude of the bonus is equal to +1, +1 per 4 points of your base attack bonus, no matter how many times you miss enemies or they make their saves against your spells after that.
For every +1 bonus you gain, you also take a –1 penalty to Armor Class. This penalty disappears when the bonus no longer applies.
Source: This emulates the Mark of CaniaFCII feat.

sections.heading: Feint, DisengagingUC [Skill]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Bluff 1 rank.
Benefit: As a standard action, use Bluff to feint against an opponent. Instead of denying that opponent its Dex bonus to AC, a successful feint allows you to move up to your speed without provoking an attack of opportunity from the opponent you feinted (for leaving the square you start in).
If you have at least 6 ranks in Bluff, if you succeed at a Bluff check to feint in combat, the feinted opponent can’t make attacks of opportunity against you until the start of its next turn. This subsumes the Timely Misdirection skill trickCSc.If you have at least 6 ranks in Bluff, as a standard action you can make a Bluff check against all opponents currently threatening you. If you succeed against at least one opponent, you can move up to your speed as part of that standard action. This movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity from any opponent you succeeded at feinting against.If you have at least 11 ranks in Bluff, whenever you use this ability, you can make a single melee attack against one opponent you succeeded at feinting against. That opponent is denied his Dexterity bonus to AC against this attack.If you have at least 16 ranks in Bluff, you can make a full attack as you disengage; opponents you succeeded in Bluffing are denied their Dex bonuses to AC against these attacks.
Source: This feat also subsumes the Disengaging Flourish and Disengaging Shot featsUC.

sections.heading: Feint, Improved [Finesse, Skill]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Weapon Finesse, Bluff 1 rank.
Benefit: You can make a Bluff check to feint in combat as a move action. In addition to feinting normally, you can instead choose to feint defensively (the so-called “baffling defense”), using your Bluff results in place of your AC for the next attack made against you.
Your ability to feint continues to improve with your skill in Bluff, as follows:
If you have at least 6 ranks in Bluff, whenever you use feint to cause an opponent to lose his Dexterity bonus, he loses that bonus against all threatening opponents until the beginning of your next turn, in addition to losing his Dexterity bonus against your next attack. If you use baffling defense, you can use your Bluff results against all attacks you are aware of that round.If you have at least 11 ranks in Bluff, you can feint in combat (offensively or using the baffling defense) as a swift action. When feinting as a partial action, you can perform a group fake-out (see Bluff skill) without taking the normal penalty for feinting against multiple opponents.If you have at least 16 ranks in Bluff, all opponents with CMD less than 10 + your Bluff skill bonus automatically lose their Dex bonus to AC against your attacks.
Special: In addition to the above benefits, you gain a +2 competence bonus with other tricky maneuvers (as described in Chapter 1); thus bonus increases by +1 per 4 ranks in Bluff you possess.
Normal: Feinting in combat is a standard action, and is always offensive. Creatures you feint lose their Dexterity bonus against your next attack only.
Source: This feat subsumes the Greater Feint featCRB, the Surprising Riposte featDU, the Invisible Blade’s “uncanny feint” prestige class featureCW, and the Swordsage’s baffling defense counterToB.

sections.heading: Fight OnAPG
sections.text:
You call on deep reserves to continue fighting.
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: You can Take a Breather (Chapter 7) as a standard action, rather than a full-round action. If you are already at full hp, you can use the healing function to gain temporary hit points instead; these last up to 1 minute per character level, or until lost.
If your BAB is at least +6, you can take a breather as a partial action.If your BAB is at least +11, you can take a breather as a move action.If your BAB is at least +16, you can take a breather as a swift action.
You can still Take a Breather only once per encounter.
Normal: Taking a Breather is a fill-round action, and does not prfovide temporary hp.
Source: This feat also supersedes the Increased Vigor and Greater Increased Vigor featsCBEM.

sections.heading: Flanking, Improved
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: When you provide or receive an Aid Another attack bonus in combat (Chapter 7), the total bonus improves by +1. For every 4 points of your base attack bonus, this bonus improves by an additional +1 (maximum total bonus of +8 at BAB +20).
If your BAB is at least +6, allies for whom you provide an Aid Another bonus to attacks deal an additional 1d6 points of precision damage with each successful melee attack against the flanked opponent (this does not stack with existing sneak attack ability possessed by them, if any).If your BAB is at least +11, your allies gain +2d6 damage, rather than +1d6.If your BAB is at least +16, your allies gain +3d6 damage, rather than +1d6.
Synergy:
A bonded animal companion with this feat can use half of its master’s number of ranks in Handle Animal in place of its Charisma modifier when calculating its Bluff bonus when feinting; this supersedes the Ferocious Feint featUW.When combined with the Distracting Strike feat (q.v.), this feat supersedes the Nightsong Infiltrator’s “teamwork sneak attack” prestige class featureCA.
Normal: An Aid Another bonus in combat provides a flat +2 bonus on attacks (or +1 for additional aid), and no damage bonus unless the sneak attack ability is possessed.
Source: This feat supersedes the Swashbuckler class feature of the same nameCW, and the Great TeamworkOA, Improved AidOA, Precise AssaultAPG, Precise StrikeAPG, Superior FlankingDr343, and Vexing FlankerPHII feats.

sections.heading: Giant-Slayer
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1, Acrobatics 5 ranks; or dwarf or Small sized race.
Benefit: You gain a +4 dodge bonus to your Armor Class against giants, or a +1 dodge bonus against any non-giant creature two or more size categories larger than yourself. This benefit does not apply if you lose your Dex bonus to AC, or if your speed is reduced by wearing armor.
You also gain a +1 racial bonus to attacks and damage against creatures at least one size category larger than you are.
For every 4 points of your base attack bonus, these racial modifiers increase by +1, to a maximum AC bonus of +9 vs. giants (+6 vs. others), and maximum attack and damage bonuses of +6.
Synergy: If you also have one or more Improved Combat Maneuvers feats, you can treat opponents larger than you as if they were smaller when attempting appropriate maneuvers against them. This effective reduction reduces the opponent’s size bonus to CMB and CMD against you (this does not stack with the racial bonus to attacks granted to you by this feat), and also permits you to perform maneuvers such as trip against opponents that would normally be too large to affect, as follows:
BAB | Effective Size Reduction
+1 | 1 step (e.g., Huge to Large)
+6 | 2 steps (e.g., Gargantuan to Large)
+11 | 3 steps (e.g., Colossal to Large)
+16 | 4 steps (e.g., Colossal to Medium)

You gain additional advantages if you meet a minimum number of ranks in Acrobatics, as follows:
If your BAB is at least +6 and you have at least 6 ranks in Acrobatics (or are a gnome with BAB +6), and you successfully use the Acrobatics skill enter the space of a creature at least one size larger than you are without provoking an attack of opportunity, then while you and that opponent continue to occupy the same space the opponent is treated as being flat-footed to your attacks.If your BAB is +11 or higher and you have at least 11 ranks in Acrobatics (or are a dwarf or gnome with BAB +11), you gain 50% cover against all attacks (+4 shield bonus to AC and Reflex saves), including those made by the creature whose space you’re in, when sharing the space of a creature at least one size larger than you are.
Source: This feat supersedes the Gnome Giant-SlayerCW “Crafty Fighter” prestige class feature. The expanded use of the feat simulates the wolf climbs the mountain and giant killing style maneuversToB; the Low Blow and Improved Low Blow featsRF; and the Earth Child Topple featUC.

sections.heading: Initiative, Improved
sections.text:
Steven drew his guns so fast I never saw his hands move. Lightning ain't in it, dear. At one moment those revolvers with their big sandalwood grips were by his sides; at the next he was blazing away...
―Stephen King, The Wind through the Keyhole (2012)
Your quick reflexes allow you to react quickly to danger.
Benefit: You gain a +4 competence bonus on initiative checks.

sections.heading: Initiative, SuperiorSRD
sections.text:
Benefit: You gain a +2 insight bonus on initiative checks.
Special: You may select this feat multiple times; each time, increase the bonus by an additional +2.
Source: This feat supersedes the duelist’s Improved Reaction prestige class feature, the “gunslinger initiative” class featureUC, and the Reactionary combat traitAPG.

sections.heading: Inspirational Victory
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1, Knowledge (warfare) 1 rank.
Benefit: Once per encounter as a swift action, you may designate an opponent who represents a credible threat (see above) as the target of this feat. If you reduce that enemy to fewer than 0 hp during that encounter, your allies are heartened, and gain a morale bonus equal to half your base attack bonus (minimum +1) on all damage rolls for the remainder of the encounter.
Source: This feat simulates the lion’s roar boostToB.

sections.heading: Lead the ChargeToB [Skill]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1, Knowledge (warfare) 1 rank.
Benefit: Whenever you personally lead a charge, other charging allies within 60 ft. who can hear your voice gain a +1 circumstance bonus to attacks made at the end of their charge. This bonus increases by +1 per 4 ranks in Knowledge (warfare) you possess. Affected allies gain a competence bonus to speed while charging equal to 5 ft. x the attack bonus granted by this feat, as shown in the table.
In addition, each affected ally deals bonus damage on his or her first successful charge attack as shown in the table below, based on number of ranks in Knowledge (warfare), whichever is lower. This bonus damage is not multiplied on a successful critical hit.
You can use this feat only once per encounter.
Skill Ranks | Attack | Damage | Speed
+1 to +3 | +1 | +0 | +5 ft.
+4 to +7 | +2 | +1d6 | +10 ft.
+8 to +11 | +3 | +2d6 | +15 ft.
+12 to +15 | +4 | +3d6 | +20 ft.
+16 to +19 | +5 | +4d6 | +25 ft.
+20 | +6 | +5d6 | +30 ft.
Source: This feat also supersedes the Marshal’s over the top auraMH and the Battle Herald’s sound the charge commandAPG.

sections.heading: Mobility [Skill]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Acrobatics 1 rank, Dodge.
Benefit: You are trained in moving during combat. You gain the following benefits:
You gain a dodge bonus equal to your number of ranks in Acrobatics to AC against attacks of opportunity caused when you move out of or within a threatened area. When charging or skirmishing, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your attack roll per 10 feet of movement taken immediately before an attack.The bonus from your Dodge feat also applies to saving throws or checks against [inertia] and [restraint] effects (Chapter 7). If you have at least 16 ranks in Acrobatics, you gain a perpetual freedom of movement effect as an extraordinary (Ex) ability
Source: This subsumes the feat of the same nameCRB, and also the Mobile Fighter archetypeAPG.

sections.heading: Mounted Combat [Skill]
sections.text:
You are adept at fighting from horseback and at guiding your mount through combat.
Prerequisites: Handle Animal 1 rank.
Benefit: While you are mounted, you and your mount receive a +1 circumstance bonus to damage against opponents adjacent to your mount. This bonus increases by an additional +1 per 5 ranks in Handle Animal thereafter (maximum +4 at 16 ranks).
If you have at least 6 ranks in Handle Animal, when your mount is hit in combat, you may spend an immediate action to attempt a Handle Animal check to negate the hit. The hit is negated if your check result is greater than the opponent’s attack roll.
If you do nothing else while mounted (you cannot attack when riding defensively), you gain a +2 bonus on Reflex saves and a +4 dodge bonus to AC. In addition, your mount gains a +20 ft. bonus to its speed, a +2 bonus on all Will saves, and a +4 dodge bonus to its Armor Class.
If you have at least 11 ranks in Handle Animal, you can also choose to make Handle Animal checks in place of your mount’s saving throws, at the same action cost. If you have at least 16 ranks in Handle Animal, you and your mount suffer no armor check penalty on skill checks while mounted. When charging, you may jump from you mount toward your target. If you jump 10 feet, your charge modifiers on attack rolls and to AC are doubled and you are still considered mounted for purposes of damage, mounted combat feats, and so on. This supersedes the Dragoon’s “leaping lance” abilityUC.
Synergy: Mounted Combat can be combined with other feats in various ways:
If you have the Improved Overrun feat, you can perform overrun maneuvers using your mount. When calculating the CMB, use the mount’s size modifier. Apply your base attack bonus and Strength bonus or your mount’s, whichever is higher. When you attempt to overrun an opponent while mounted, your target cannot choose to avoid you. Your mount may make one hoof attack against any target you knock down, gaining the standard +4 bonus on attack rolls against prone targets. These benefits supersede the Trample feat.If you also have the Improved Bull Rush feat, when charging an opponent while mounted and wielding a lance, resolve the attack as normal. If it hits, you may immediately make a free bull rush attempt in addition to the normal damage. If successful, the target is knocked off his horse and lands prone in a space adjacent to his mount that is directly away from you. If you have the Improved Weapon Maneuvers feat and your base attack bonus is +6 or higher, you can make a check, disarm, or sunder maneuver as a free action any time you successfully perform a mounted charge against an opponent. This free combat maneuver does not provoke an attack of opportunity.If you have the Skirmish feat, the benefits apply to both you and your mount (including hoof attacks made while overrunning an opponent, if applicable). You can make a full attack from a galloping mount.
Source: This feat now subsumes the Pathfinder Trample and Unhorse feats; the roughrider fighter’s Mounted Mettle variant class featureAPG; part of the cavalier’s Mighty Charge class featureAPG; and also the Power of the SteedBEM and Indomitable MountPoP feats.

sections.heading: No Retreat
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: Whenever a foe within reach attempts to take a 5-foot step away from you, you may also make a 5-foot or 10-foot step as an immediate action, so long as you end up adjacent to the foe that triggered this ability. This ability can be used against only one opponent per turn.
If your BAB is +6 or higher, when using this feat to follow an opponent, you receive an attack of opportunity against that opponent, if the movement from this feat puts you within reach. Against enemies you threaten that take a withdraw action, you can choose to forego pursuit and instead make an immediate attack of opportunity. If your BAB is +11 or greater, you can move any distance up to your normal speed in pursuit, rather than being limited to 10 feet. This movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity.
Normal: You gain no free movement against foes who step away. The withdraw action does not provoke attacks of opportunity.
Sources: This feat supersedes the duelist prestige class feature of the same nameCRB, and also the Step Up featCRB, and the Following Step and Step Up and Strike featsAPG. It also emulates the Swordsage’s mirrored pursuit and stalking shadow countersToB.

sections.heading: Opportunist, Draw AttackCBEM
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Dex 15, Bluff 1 rank, Combat Reflexes.
Benefit: When an opponent makes an attack of opportunity against you, you can make an attack of opportunity against that foe as an immediate action.
Synergy:
If you also have the Improved Feint feat, you can feint so as to intentionally provoke an attack of opportunity from one melee opponent. If your enemy takes advantage of this opportunity, you gain an immediate counterattack as noted above. The target of this feat is permitted an opposed Bluff check (against your feint) to see the feigned opening for what it is.If you have the Distracting Strike feat, you can activate it automatically as part of the attack of opportunity you gain from the use of this feat, even if the normal conditions are not met.If your BAB is +16 or higher and you have the Improved Critical and Killing Stroke feats (q.v.), as a full attack you can allow one target in melee to deliver a coup de grâce against you as if you were helpless (the target must still hit you, is subject to any miss chance it would normally have against you, and may decide to forego the attack in any event). If the target decides to take this opening and hits you, you may immediately attempt a single coup de grâce attack against it as if it were helpless (even if the opponent’s attack simultaneously incapacitates or kills you). Your coup de grâce requires a roll to hit but is not subject to any miss chances, for you are using your target's attack as a guide for your own attack, even if the target is invisible, in total darkness, under the effects of a displacement spell, and so on. You and your target still provoke attacks of opportunity from threatening opponents as normal.
Source: This feat also subsumes the Swordsage’s feigned opening counterToB, the Broken Wing Gambit and Panther Style featsUC, the orc Reverse-Feint featARG, and the Reciprocal Slaying feat from Sean K Reynolds’ web site.

sections.heading: Power Attack
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Str 13, base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: You can choose to take a –1 penalty on all melee attack rolls and combat maneuver checks to gain a +2 circumstance bonus on all melee damage rolls. This bonus to damage is increased by half (+50%) if you are making an attack with a two-handed weapon, a one handed weapon using two hands, or a primary natural weapon that adds 1½ times your Strength modifier on damage rolls. This bonus to damage is halved (–50%) if you are making an attack with a light manufactured weapon, or an off-hand weapon or secondary natural weapon.
When your base attack bonus reaches +4, and every 4 points thereafter, the penalty increases by –1 and the bonus to damage increases by +2. You must choose to use this feat before making an attack roll, and its effects last until your next turn. The bonus damage does not apply to touch attacks or effects that do not deal hit point damage.

sections.heading: Power Attack, Furious FocusAPG
sections.text:
Even in the midst of fierce and furious blows, you can find focus in the carnage and your seemingly wild blows strike home.
Prerequisites: Str 13, Power Attack.
Benefit: When you are wielding a two-handed weapon or a one-handed weapon with two hands, and using the Power Attack feat, you do not suffer Power Attack’s penalty on melee attack rolls on the first attack you make each turn. You still suffer the penalty on any additional attacks, including attacks of opportunity.

sections.heading: Practiced Fighter
sections.text:
Prerequisite: At least one fighter talent.
Benefit: Treat your effective fighter level as 4 higher than is actually the case, to a maximum effective fighter level equal to your total hit dice. This applies to your weapon training class feature, and also when determining the effects of fighter talents such as Armor Training. It does not grant you additional fighter talents or feats, more advanced fighter talents, or any other benefits of the fighter class.
Special: Apply this feat after any class synergy features improving your effective fighter level. The effects stack (this is a specific exception to the non-stacking rule). Your total limit based on effective character level, as described in Chapter 1, remains in force.

sections.heading: Press the AdvantageToB
sections.text:
Benefit: Whenever you take a 5-ft. step, you can also take one additional 5-ft. step as a free action as long as you then end your movement for the round.
You can instead take a single 5-ft. step into difficult terrain, but cannot then take the second 5-ft. step.

sections.heading: Reflexes, Combat
sections.text:
You can make additional attacks of opportunity and other immediate actions.
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: The maximum number of immediate actions you can take in a round is equal to 1 + your Dexterity bonus (or 1 + the number derived from your base attack bonus, whichever is higher). You gain additional options depending on your base attack bonus, as follows:
If your BAB is at least +6, you may make an attack of opportunity whenever an opponent you threaten draws a weapon, readies or looses a shield, or attempts to feint in combat (even with the Improved Feint feat). You are able to make attacks of opportunity even when you are flat-footed.If your BAB is at least +11, your successful attacks of opportunity interfere with the actions that provoked them. Those actions are not completed, but are not lost, either; they can be re-attempted immediately (which likely provokes an additional attack of opportunity from you). You can make attacks of opportunity (when provoked) even against foes with cover (but not total cover).If your BAB is at least +16, there is no limit to the number of immediate actions you can make in one round. You still can’t make more than one attack of opportunity or other immediate action for a given opportunity, however. You can make attacks of opportunity even against opponents with total concealment.
Synergy:
If you have this feat and at least one Strike feat (q.v.), you can add the effects of one [strike] to an attack of opportunity. If you do so, you cannot make more than one attack of opportunity that round.If you are trained in Planar Sense as a class skill, any creature using a Conjuration effect to enter or leave a square threatened by you provokes an attack of opportunity, even if casting defensively or using a supernatural ability. This supersedes the Teleport Tactician featAPG.
Special: This feat does not allow more than one counterattack using the Riposte fighter talent.
Normal: A character without this feat can make only the number immediate actions allowed by his or her base attack bonus (Chapter 7). You cannot make attacks of opportunity while flat-footed, or against an opponent with partial cover or total concealment.
Source: This feat also subsumes the Epic Combat ReflexesSRD, Canny OpportunistDr340, and Deft OpportunistCAd feats; the Warblade’s “battle mastery” class featureToB; and the “exotic reach” Exotic Weapon Master stuntCW. Paired with the Staggering Strike feat, it subsumes the Flowing MonkUC “unbalancing counter.” Paired with the Vital Strike feat, it subsumes the Impressive Cleave featCBEM.

sections.heading: Shatter Defenses [Skill]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: BAB +6, Bluff 6 ranks, Staredown.
Benefit: You treat any opponent under a [fear] condition (Chapter 7) as flat-footed to your attacks.
If your BAB is +11 or greater and you have at least 11 ranks in Bluff, creatures within your reach who start their turns with a [fear] condition provoke attacks of opportunity from you.
Synergy: If you have the Vital Strike feat, it always applies against flat-footed opponents, even on a full attack.
Source: This feat also subsumes the Avenging Executioner’s “dread blade” prestige class featureCSc and the Imperious Command featDU.

sections.heading: Skirmish
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Dex 13, base attack bonus +6, Dodge.
Benefit: You can move your full speed and still make a full attack that round. Because this is a full attack, abilities that require a single attack as a standard action do not apply (except as described hereafter).
With this feat, you also gain the “pounce” ability, allowing you to move twice your normal speed on a charge and make a full attack at the end.
Synergy: If you also have the Vital Strike feat and fulfill the following conditions, you can apply your Vital Strike damage to iterative attacks while moving (but not other [strike] feats, nor improvements to Vital Strike damage from the Mountain Hammer talent):
You must use your full movement and all your attacks on your turn (without holding or foregoing any movement or attacks);You must move at least 5 ft. between attacks, unless you also have the Spring Attack feat;Movement must be generally in a straight line (with no turn of more than 45 degrees), unless you also have the Spring Attack feat.
Additional Vital Strike damage applies only against creatures that have not yet acted that round. This extra damage applies to ranged attacks, but only if the target is within point blank range (normally 30 feet, although this can be expanded with the Point-Blank Shot feat).
Synergy: If you also have the Mounted Combat feat, you can use this feat while mounted, using your mount’s speed rather than yours.
Source: This feat supersedes the ScoutCAd and the Highland StalkerCAd class feature of the same name. It also subsumes the Flyby Attack, Ride-By Attack, Shot on the RunCRB and Dire ChargeSRD feats.

sections.heading: Spring Attack
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Dex 13, Acrobatics 6 ranks, Dodge.
Benefit: You can freely interspace movement and attacks, as long as any movement taken is in 5-ft. increments, and the total does not exceed half your speed (or your full speed, if you also have the Skirmish feat). Movement can be in any direction you choose, including backwards.
If your BAB is +6 or greater, opponents targeted by your attacks cannot make attacks of opportunity against you in response to your movement.If your BAB is at least +11 and you have at least 5 ft. of movement in reserve as a held action, you can use this movement to take a 5-ft. step as an immediate action to remove yourself from a threatened square. Done in response to an attack, this can actually cause the attack to miss, whistling through the space you just vacated.
Special: When you charge, you can make turns of up to 90 degrees during your movement. All other restrictions on charges still apply; for instance, you cannot pass through a square that blocks or slows movement, or that contains a creature (unless you have the Improved Overrun feat and overrun that creature). You must have line of sight to the opponent at the start of your turn.
Source: This feat now subsumes the Bounding Assault and Rapid Blitz featsPHII, and also the Focused ChargeSRD feat and the shifting defense maneuverToB.

sections.heading: Staredown [Skill]
sections.text:
A sheep might gaze at you without transmitting a warning through your subjective mind, because you are in no danger from a sheep. But let a tiger gaze fixedly at you from ambush, and unless your primitive instincts are completely calloused you will presently commence to glance furtively about and be filled with vague, unreasoning terror.
―Edgar Rice Burroughs, Pellucidar (1915)
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1, Bluff 1 rank.
Benefit: As a standard action, you can make a demoralize check (see Bluff skill) against all foes within 30 feet who can see you, without the normal “mass demoralize” penalty.
As your base attack bonus and number of ranks in Bluff improve, the speed at which you can intimidate nearby opponents also improves, as described below.
If your BAB is +6 or higher and you have at least 6 ranks in Bluff, you can demoralize opponents within 30 ft. as a partial action. If your BAB is +11 or higher and you have at least 11 ranks in Bluff, you can demoralize opponents within 30 ft. as a move action. If your BAB is at least +16 and you have at least 16 ranks in Bluff, you gain the frightful presence (Ex) ability. When you draw a weapon, charge, or are in a rage, your Staredown automatically affects opponents within 30 ft., without requiring an action on your part. You are assumed to be taking 10; so that the DC to resist each condition is as follows:
Condition | DC to Resist
Cowering | Your Bluff bonus -10
Panicked | Your Bluff bonus -5
Frightened | Your Bluff bonus
Shaken | 10 + your Bluff bonus
Synergy:
If you have at least 6 ranks in Bluff and also have the Killing Stroke feat (q.v.), whenever you reduce an enemy to 0 or fewer hit points (whether using Killing Stroke or not), you can also make a Bluff check to demoralize all enemies within 30 feet as a free action. Enemies that cannot see both you and the enemy you struck are unaffected. This subsumes the Dreadful CarnageAPG, Mortifying AttackCR, and Gory FinishUC feats, the Fountain of Blood boostToB, and the Ghost-Face KillerCAd “frightful attack” and Avenging ExcutionerCSc “bloody murder” prestige class features.Instead of only affecting targets who can see you, you can also affect creatures within a darkness effect you create (you can cast darkness and also use this ability as a single full-round action). This supersedes the Nightmare Weaver featUC. A bonded animal companion with this feat can use half of its master’s number of ranks in Handle Animal in place of its Charisma modifier when calculating its Bluff bonus to demoralize; this supersedes the Ferocious Beast featUW.Creatures larger than Medium with the frightful presence ability have a wider radius than 30 ft., as follows:
Creature Size | Frightful Presence Radius
Medium or smaller | 30 ft.
Large | 40 ft.
Huge | 60 ft.
Gargantuan | 90 ft.
Colossal | 120 ft.

Normal: Demoralizing multiple opponents applies a -2 penalty per individual to be demoralized. Demoralizing is a standard action (see Bluff skill). Targets of demoralization attempts must be within 30 ft.
Source: This feat supersedes the Dazzling Display featCRB and much of the Samurai classCW. It also subsumes the Avenging Executioner’s “rapid intimidation” prestige class featureCSc and the Never Outnumbered skill trickCSc.

sections.heading: Stone PowerToB
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: When attacking, you can take a -1 penalty to your attack rolls, with an additional -1 per 4 points of your base attack bonus. In exchange, you gain temporary hit points equal to 1d6 x the number that you subtract from your attack rolls. These temporary hit points last until the beginning of your next turn.

sections.heading: Unskittering Attack
sections.text: Benefit: Your attacks ignore up to 2 points of deflection bonus to the target’s AC (if any). For every 4 points of your base attack bonus, your attacks ignore an additional point of deflection bonus (maximum +7 deflection ignored at BAB +20).

sections.heading: Venom, Fast-Acting
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Poison special attack.
Benefit: Your poison acts more quickly than normal. Reduce the onset time and duration time step by 1 unit (hours become minutes; minutes become rounds). An onset time of 1 round can be reduced to immediate in this manner; duration steps between saves cannot be reduced below 1 round.
Special: You can gain this feat multiple times. Each time, reduce onset and duration by 1 step.

sections.heading: Venom, Virulent
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Poison special attack.
Benefit: The effects of your poison are more difficult to shake off. A “cure” listing of 1 save instead requires 2 saves. A cure of 2 saves instead requires 2 consecutive saves. A poison that already requires 2 consecutive saves cannot be further affected by this feat.
Special: You can gain this feat twice, in order to change a cure of “1 save” to “2 consecutive saves.”

sections.heading: Venomous Natural AttackFC
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Con 13+, natural weapons.
Benefit: A number of times per day equal to your Constitution modifier, you can secrete poison onto one set of your natural weapons (bite, or claws, etc.) as a swift action. This poison remains in place until you damage a target with that weapon. Any creature struck must succeed on a Fort save (DC 10 + half your Hit Dice + your Con modifier) or be poisoned. You are immune to your own poison. The poison you secrete cannot be collected or preserved.
Poison—injury, damage 1d2 Strength per round; duration 6 rounds; cure 1 save.
Special: You can gain this feat multiple times. Each time, it applies to a different mode of natural attacks.

sections.heading: Combat Feats, Armor/Shield
sections.text: As with general combat feats, all feats in this section have the [Combat] descriptor.

sections.heading: Armor Proficiency, Heavy
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Light Armor Proficiency, Medium Armor Proficiency.
Benefit: You are proficient with heavy armor.
Normal: See Armor Proficiency, Light.
Special: Fighters and paladins automatically have Heavy Armor Proficiency as a bonus feat (unless they trade it for some other benefit).

sections.heading: Armor Proficiency, Light
sections.text:
Benefit: When you wear a type of armor with which you are proficient, the armor check penalty for that armor applies only to Dexterity- and Strength-based skill checks.
Normal: A character who is wearing armor with which he is not proficient applies its armor check penalty to attack rolls and to all skill checks that involve moving.
Special: All PC classes except the monk, sorcerer, and wizard, automatically include Light Armor Proficiency as a bonus feat (unless it is traded for some other benefit; see individual class descriptions).

sections.heading: Armor Proficiency, Medium
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Light Armor Proficiency.
Benefit: You are proficient with medium armor.
Normal: See Armor Proficiency, Light.
Special: Barbarians, bards (skalds only), clerics, druids, fighters, inquisitors, paladins, and rangers automatically have Medium Armor Proficiency as a bonus feat (unless they trade it for some other benefit; see individual class descriptions).

sections.heading: Armor Training, Arcane [Arcane, Skill]
sections.text:
You have learned how to cast spells while wearing armor.
Prerequisites: Armor proficiency, Concentration 1 rank.
Benefit: When wearing armor with which you are proficient, you treat that armor’s arcane spell failure chance as if it were 10% lower than actual. If you possess a sufficiently high base attack bonus and number of ranks in Concentration, greater reductions in spell failure are possible, according to the following table.
Minimum: | Spell Failure Reduction
Skill Ranks | Base Attack
1 | +0 | 10%
6 | +6 | 20%
11 | +11 | 30%
16 | +16 | 40%
Special: This feat does not apply to armor and shields separately. If you wear armor and carry a shield, first total the arcane spell failure chance, then apply the effects of this feat.

sections.heading: Armored TrapIH
sections.text:
You constantly prepare counterattacks against opponents, timing your attacks to connect just as your armor baffles theirs.
Prerequisites: Heavy armor proficiency.
Benefit: When wearing armor and using a held attack (Chapter 7) against an opponent attacking you in melee, you gain a circumstance bonus to your attack equal to your armor training bonus (if any), and a circumstance bonus to damage equal to the AC bonus you receive from the armor (maximum +1 per point of your base attack bonus).

sections.heading: Block ArrowHB
sections.text:
You can block incoming arrows with your shield.
Prerequisite: Dex 13, Martial shield proficiency.
Benefit: To use this feat, you must be actively using a shield (not merely an animated shield or a shield spell). When you would normally be hit with a ranged weapon, you can spend an immediate action to deflect it so that you take no damage from it. You must be aware of the attack. Unusually massive ranged weapons, such as boulders hurled by giants and siege weapon attacks, can't be deflected.
Synergy:
If you also have the Shield Cover feat, you can parry ranged touch spells and attacks (such as rays) as if they were weapon attacks. If you have the Armor Training fighter talent, this feat is superseded by the more general Shield Parry feat (q.v.).
Source: This feat also supersedes the Missile Shield and Ray Shield featsAPG.

sections.heading: Sacrificial Shield
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Martial shield proficiency.
Benefit: When you are struck in combat while using a shield, you can spend an immediate action to apply the damage to your shield. Subtract your shield's hardness and hit points (Chapter 6) from the damage of the attack; you take only the remainder (if any).
If the shield takes enough damage to destroy it, it's destroyed. Otherwise, it gains the broken condition, even if the damage was not enough to give it the broken condition under other circumstances.
Synergy: If you also have the Shared Shield feat, you can use this ability to protect an adjacent ally.
Source: This feat emulates the 2nd tier Guardian ability of the same nameMA.

sections.heading: Shield Bash, Improved
sections.text:
You can protect yourself with your shield, even if you use it to attack.
Prerequisites: Exotic Shield Proficiency, Two-Weapon Fighting.
Benefit: When you perform a shield bash, you may still apply the shield’s shield bonus to your AC.
If your BAB is at least +6, when shield bashing with a magic shield, your shield’s enhancement bonus to AC can be applied as an enhancement bonus to attacks and damage as well. The maximum enhancement bonus that can be applied in this manner is equal to +1 per 4 points of your base attack bonus. If your BAB is at least +11, your shield bash deals damage as if your shield were one size larger (1d4 for a light shield, 1d6 for a heavy shield; or 1d6 for a light spiked shield, 1d8 for a heavy spiked shield). This does not stack with the bashing shield property.If your BAB is at least +16, when fighting with a shield, you can make normal weapon attacks (with the two-weapon fighting penalty) but hold your shield bashes (Chapter 7 – held actions). Any time before your next turn, when you are attacked by an opponent, you can spend an immediate action to make one of the held shield bashes against that opponent; if this bash damages the target, the attack that triggered it misses. This simulates the Crusader’s shield counter maneuverToB.
SpecialAA: You can also force your shield into the mouth of a creature to prevent it from using bite attacks or other mouth-based abilities. Make a grapple check against a creature at least two sizes larger than your size category. If you succeed, you wedge your shield into its mouth. At any time you may release your shield, which means you both lose the grappled condition and return to your own squares, though your shield remains in its mouth. The creature may remove the shield by destroying it (or leaving it with the broken condition), forcing the shield out of its mouth with a grapple check against your CMB, or swallowing it (if it has the swallow whole ability) as if the shield were a creature.
While the shield is in place, the monster cannot use its mouth to make attacks (such as a bite or a giant frog’s sticky tongue) against anything but the shield and cannot speak clearly enough to cast spells or use items requiring speech. If it uses a breath weapon, its range is half normal and any damage dealt must first get through the shield, with any remaining damage affecting the area normally.
Synergy: If you also have the Improved Bull Rush feat, any opponents hit by your shield bash are also hit with a free bull rush attack, substituting your attack roll for the combat maneuver check. This bull rush does not provoke an attack of opportunity. Opponents who cannot move back due to a wall or other surface are knocked prone after moving the maximum possible distance. You may choose to move with your target if you are able to take a 5-foot step or to spend an action to move this turn. This supersedes the Shield Slam feat from the core rules.
Normal: Without this feat, a character that performs a shield bash loses the shield’s shield bonus to AC until his next turn. Magic shields do not apply their enhancement bonus to shield bashes.

sections.heading: Shield Cover
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Martial Shield Proficiency.
Benefit: When actively using a light, heavy, or tower shield (not a buckler, animated shield, or shield spell), your shield bonus (and any enhancement bonus it possessed) apply to your touch AC.
If your BAB is at least +6, you retain your shield bonuses while flat-footed. In addition, you may apply your shield bonus to Reflex saves (in the latter case, the shield’s enhancement bonus does not stack with resistance bonuses to Reflex saves, if any).If your BAB is at least +11, your shield bonus applies to your CMD as well.If your BAB is at least +16, when using a shield you are immune to effects that normally auto-confirm critical hits against you (Cf. Improved Critical).
Normal: Shield bonuses do not apply to flat-footed or touch AC, nor to CMD or reflex saves.
Source: This feat subsumes the Parrying ShieldLoM, Shield WardPHII, Shield SpecializationAPG feats, and the Knight of the Realm’s knightly defenseRRE.

sections.heading: Shield Parry
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Martial Shield Proficiency, Armor Training, base attack bonus +6.
Benefit: When actively using a shield (not an animated shield or a shield spell) you can use it to attempt one parry per round (Chapter 7) as an immediate action against an incoming attack. Penalties for Two-Weapon Fighting apply normally, but bonuses for Armor Training also apply.
Synergy:
If you also have the Shield Cover feat (q.v.), you can parry ranged touch spells and attacks as if they were weapon attacks. If your BAB is at least +11 and you use a magical shield to successfully parry an incoming ranged touch spell or attack (including a ray), you can redirect the effect at any target within the attack’s remaining range, including the original caster. Use the original spell’s attack roll, save DC, etc.If you also have the Blind-Fight feat, you master the art of using the reflective surface of your shield to locate foes that you dare not look at directlyAA. On your turn, you may choose to forfeit your shield’s AC bonus for 1 round to improve your defenses against one creature using a gaze attack (if you also have the Improved Shield Bash feat, you can use this trick without losing the AC bonus). Your chance to avoid having to make a saving throw against that creature’s gaze attack increases to 100%, and the creature does not gain concealment against you. For every 5 ranks in Perception you have, you may simultaneously use this ability against one additional creature with a gaze attack.
Source: This feat replaces the Improved Shield Specialization and Reflective Shield featsCBEM.

sections.heading: Shield Proficiency, Martial
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1, Simple Shield Proficiency.
Benefit: You gain Martial proficiency with all shields (Chapter 6).
Special: Barbarians, clerics, fighters, and paladins automatically have Martial Shield Proficiency as a bonus feat. They need not select it.

sections.heading: Shield Proficiency, Simple
sections.text:
You are trained in how to properly use shields.
Benefit: Simple proficiency with all shields.
Normal: When you are using a shield with which you are not proficient, you take the shield’s armor check penalty on attack rolls and on all Strength- and Dexterity-related skill checks.
Special: Bards, druids, incarnates, and rogues automatically have Simple Shield Proficiency as a bonus feat. They need not select it.

sections.heading: Shield Proficiency, Exotic
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Simple Shield Proficiency.
Benefit: Select one shield. You gain Exotic proficiency with that shield (Chapter 6).

sections.heading: Combat Feats, Weapon-and Style-Specific
sections.text: The feats presented here are specific to certain weapons and/or combat styles, including dueling (finesse weapons), two-weapon fighting, and unarmed combat. Descriptors such as [Unarmed] and [Ranged] are provided for ease of reference; as with general combat feats, all feats in this section have the [Combat] descriptor, in addition to any others listed.

sections.heading: AxefightingCBEM [Axe, Slashing]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Dex 13, base attack bonus +1, Weapon Specialization (any axe).
Benefit: Whenever you drop a foe (i.e., reduce him below 0 hp) with a qualifying axe, you gain a +2 morale bonus to attacks and damage with your weapon for 1 round, plus 1 round per 5 points of your base attack bonus above +1 (e.g., 4 rounds total at BAB +16).

sections.heading: Backswing [Two-Handed]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Str 13, base attack bonus +6, Overhand Chop.
Benefit: When using the full-attack action with a two-handed melee weapon, primary bite attack, etc., add double your Strength bonus to damage, rather than 1½ times your Strength bonus.
Normal: You normally add 1½ times your Strength modifier to damage rolls with a two-handed weapon.
Source: This feat supersedes the variant class feature of the same nameAPG, the Exotic Weapon Master’s “uncanny blow” prestige class featureCW, and the Master Samurai’s “blades of death” prestige class featureS&F.

sections.heading: Bull Rush, Improved [Maneuver]
sections.text:
“If Igli manages to put on the brakes, I’ll hit him with a low tackle and knock him in. Then we all play water polo.”	―Robert A. Heinlein, Glory Road (1963)
You are skilled at blocking your foes and pushing them around the battlefield.
Prerequisites: Str 13, Power Attack.
Benefit: You receive a +2 competence bonus on checks made to bull rush, check, drag, or reposition a foe. This bonus increases by an additional +1 per 4 points of your base attack bonus. You gain a like bonus to your CMD for defending against these maneuvers as well. You do not provoke attacks of opportunity when failing to bull rush, check, drag, or reposition an opponent.
You gain the following improvements as you gain in combat experience:
Bull Rush Strike [Strike]: If your BAB is +6 or higher, you can make a single melee attack as a standard action; if it hits, you also gain a free bull rush attempt against that opponent. At the end of this movement, the target also falls prone if a second check on your part beats his CMD. This supersedes the Bull Rush Strike and Pushing Assault featsAPG. Combining the bull rush strike with Greater Overrun (see below) allows the duplication of the Driving Attack featPHII.Greater Bull Rush: If your BAB is +11 or higher, whenever you bull rush or reposition an opponent in place of an attack (rather than in addition to an attack), the target’s movement provokes attacks of opportunity from all of your allies (but not you). This subsumes the Greater Bull Rush featCRB.Knock Back: If your BAB is +16 or higher, whenever you deal weapon damage (in hit points) greater than a melee opponent’s CMD in a single blow in melee (not including energy or spell damage), you immediately gain a special bull rush attack against that opponent as a free action. If successful, the target is pushed back 10 feet; you do not move with it unless you choose to take a 5-ft. step into the space it was formerly in. This subsumes the Knock Back featRS, CBEM.
Synergy: You can combine a bull rush with other feats in a variety of ways:
If you have medium or heavy armor proficiency, respectively, you gain a +1 armor bonus to bull rush attempts when wearing medium armor, or a +2 armor bonus when wearing heavy armor.If you have Exotic shield proficiency, you gain a +1 shield bonus to bull rush attempts when using a light shield, +2 with a heavy shield, and +3 with a tower shield.If you have the Improved Trip feat and your BAB is +6 or higher, you can attempt to overbear an opponent by making a trip attempt as an immediate action at the end of a bull rush. If you have the Improved Weapon Maneuvers feat and your BAB is +11 or higher, on a successful bull rush you slam into an opponent hard enough to make him drop whatever he’s holding (make a disarm check as a free action as the initial part of a bull rush attempt). If you have the Power Attack feat and your BAB is +6 or higher (or your Strength is 25+), a successful bull rush strike (see above) throws the victim an additional 5 feet. This supersedes the Awesome Blow featPB, the Great ThrowOA and Ki ThrowAPG feats, and the various Swordsage mighty throw strikesToB (the latter particularly if combined with Vital Strike; see below).If you have the Vital Strike feat, bull rushing a target back into a solid surface (such as a wall), rather than dealing your unarmed damage, instead inflicts Vital Strike damage plus 1½ times your Strength modifier. This supersedes part of the fighter’s “dungeon crasher” alternate class featureDS. If you have the Whirlwind Strike feat and your BAB is +6 or higher, as a full-round action you can attempt to push back (bull rush) all foes within your reach. This supersedes the Wild SwingCBEM.
Normal: Failed combat maneuvers provoke attacks of opportunity. Creatures moved by combat maneuvers do not provoke attacks of opportunity.

sections.heading: Catch Off-Guard
sections.text:
“I’ll carry my weapons right through the check-point.”
“Oh, yes, I’d forgotten about that for a moment. ‘Naked/kill’ and all that. Stab a man with a drinking straw. What a nuisance that’s been...”
―Trevanian, Shibumi (1979)
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: You do not suffer any penalties for using improvised ranged or melee weapons. Unarmed opponents are flat-footed to any attacks you make with an improvised melee weapon. You also receive a +1 competence bonus on attack rolls made with thrown splash weapons.
If your BAB is +6 or above and you have Exotic proficiency in unarmed attacks, increase the amount of damage you deal with improvised weapons by one step (for example, 1d4 becomes 1d6) to a maximum of 1d8 (2d6 if the improvised weapon is two-handed). If your BAB is at least +11, your critical threat range with improved weapons is 19–20.If your BAB is at least +16, when you confirm a critical hit with an improvised weapon, you can choose to increase the critical multiplier to x3, but the weapon itself also takes full critical damage from the attack (subject to hardness), and is therefore likely to be destroyed.
Synergy: If you have at least Martial proficiency with a light or heavy shield, you can use it as a throwing weapon with a range increment of 10 feet, dealing damage as from a shield bash. This supersedes the Shield Champion’s throw shield abilityACG.
Normal: You take a –4 penalty on attack rolls made with an improvised weapon.
Source: This feat also subsumes the Throw Anything and Improvised Weapon Mastery feats, and the “always armed” 1st tier Champion abilityMA.

sections.heading: Cloaked DuelistAotD                                 [Finesse, Maneuver, Skill]
sections.text:
You use the very cloak on your back against an enemy, befuddling their attacks.
Prerequisites: Combat Expertise, Improved Weapon Maneuvers, Weapon Finesse; Sleight of Hand 1 rank.
Benefit: When fighting with a cloak on and at least one hand empty, you may as a free action sweep your cloak into your hand to aid you in a fight, treating it as a buckler. You may instead perform Bind maneuvers with your cloak.
If your BAB is at least +6 and you have at least 6 ranks in Sleight of Hand, you can parry with your cloak as well. If you fight defensively (Chapter 7) the cloak grants you a 20% miss chance from partial concealment, as if by a blur spell (this miss chance does not stack with other concealment-based miss chances, as from the Wind Stance feat).If your BAB is at least +11 and you have at least 11 ranks in Sleight of Hand, when you use total defense (Chapter 7), your cloak grants you a 50% miss chance from concealment (as if by a displacement spell).If your BAB is at least +16 and you have at least 16 ranks in Sleight of Hand, the miss chance is 50% when fighting defensively, and you are treated as if invisible when using total defense.
Synergy:
If you also have the Improved Grapple feat, you can use your cloak to entangle an opponent on a successful grapple check. The foe can get free by using a full-round action to escape or by destroying the cape (a typical cape has hardness 1 and 3 hit points). You can use this feat with items similar in shape and weight to a cape, such as a curtain. This subsumes the Dueling Cape featACG.If you also have the Two-Weapon Fighting feat, treat your cloak as a light weapon for purposes of making off-hand binds or parries with it.

sections.heading: Clustered Attacks
sections.text:
“I'd have so much lead in his body they'd need a crane to get him off the ground.”
―Andrew H. Vachss, Hard Candy (1995)
You take a moment to carefully aim your blows or shots, causing them all to strike nearly the same spot.
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +6, Weapon Specialization. You can substitute Precise Shot for Weapon Specialization, but in that case this feat applies only to ranged attacks.
Benefit: When you use a full attack action to make multiple weapon attacks (of the type for which you meet the prerequisite) against the same opponent, total the damage from all hits before applying that opponent’s damage reduction.
Massive damage applies if the total damage you deal with this feat is equal to or exceeds half the opponent’s full normal hit points (minimum 50 points of damage).
Source: This is the Clustered ShotsUC feat, expanded for use in melee as well.

sections.heading: Critical, Improved [Critical]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1, Martial weapon proficiency.
Benefit: Choose one weapon type (e.g., longsword) with which you have at least Martial proficiency. You receive a +4 circumstance bonus on attack rolls made to confirm critical hits with that weapon.
If your BAB is +6 or higher, your threat range with the selected weapon is doubled. If your BAB is +11 or higher, all critical threats with the selected weapon are automatically confirmed.If your BAB is +16 or higher, whenever you score a critical hit with the selected weapon, the critical damage multiplier increases by 1.
Synergy: If you have at least one [Strike] feat (q.v.), you can apply the effects of that strike to any confirmed critical hit, even if none of the normal conditions were met. This has the normal effects unless otherwise noted in that feat description. You still cannot add more than one [strike] effect to a given attack unless you also have the Striking Mastery fighter talent (q.v.).
The effects of this feat do not stack with keen edge, a keen weapon, or any other effect that increases the weapon’s critical threat range, except in the case of the Versatile Unarmed Combat feat (q.v.) and the fighter’s. versatile weapon use ability (Chapter 3).
Source: This feat subsumes the feat of the same name and also the Critical Focus featCRB; the BAB +16 function subsumes the Weapon Master’s Deadly CriticalAPG and the Master Thrower prestige class’s Deadeye Shot thrown weapon trickCW.

sections.heading: Crushing BlowPHII [Bludgeoning]
sections.text:
Your bludgeoning attacks are powerful enough to damage even heavily armored foes.
Prerequisites: Weapon Specialization with a bludgeoning weapon, base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: If you miss with a bludgeoning weapon by a margin less than your opponent’s armor and/or shield bonus (if any), you batter the foe for half normal damage.
If your BAB is +6 or higher, you also ignore up to 4 points of armor bonus. If your BAB is +11 or higher, you ignore up to 8 points of your opponent’s armor bonus. Also, when you use a full attack action while fighting with any bludgeoning weapon, each attack that connects beats down your foe's defenses, granting a cumulative +2 circumstance bonus on attack rolls until the end of your current turn.If your BAB is +16 or higher, you ignore up to 12 points of your opponent’s armor bonus.
Source: This feat also subsumes the Foe Hammer expanded mastery (4) effectIH, and the Macefighter featCBEM.

sections.heading: Deadly Aim [Ranged]
sections.text:
You can make exceptionally deadly ranged attacks by pinpointing a target’s weak spot, at the expense of making the attack less likely to succeed.
Prerequisites: Wis 13, base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: You can choose to take a -1 feat penalty to ranged attacks, but gain a circumstance bonus on damage. For every 4 points of your base attack bonus, increase the attack penalty by 1 (maximum -6 at BAB +20). The bonus to damage is dependent on the type of ranged weapon you are using:
For thrown weapons, the damage bonus is equal to the magnitude of the attack penalty.For projectile weapons such as bows or slings, and for spells requiring ranged or ranged touch attack rolls (e.g., rays), you gain a +2 damage bonus per ­1 to attacks.With crossbows and firearms (despite the latter being based on ray spells), you gain a +3 damage bonus per -1 to attacks.

sections.heading: Deflect Arrows [Finesse, Unarmed]
sections.text:
You can knock arrows and other projectiles off course, preventing them from hitting you.
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1; Exotic Weapon Proficiency (unarmed attacks), Weapon Finesse, or Weapon Specialization.
Benefit: Depending on how you qualified for this feat, using it requires one of the following conditions: Exotic Proficiency (unarmed attacks)—one hand free (holding nothing); Weapon Finesse—holding manufactured finesse weapon; Weapon Specialization—wielding appropriate weapon.
Whenever you would normally be hit with a ranged weapon, you can spend an immediate action to deflect it so that you take no damage from it. You must be aware of the attack and not flat-footed. Unusually massive ranged weapons (such as boulders or ballista bolts), ranged touch attacks, and area-effect attacks can’t be deflected.
If your BAB is +6 or higher, you have at least 1 rank in Sleight of Hand, and have one hand free, instead of simply deflecting a thrown weapon, you can catch it and throw it back as an immediate action. This requires a Sleight of Hand check (DC = the results of the missile’s attack roll).If your BAB is +11 or higher, you can deflect ranged spell attacks and spell-like abilities as if they were arrows, provided the attack in question specifically targets you and requires a ranged attack roll or ranged touch attack roll. You cannot “catch” magical attacks and return them, however, unless you also have the Parry Spells fighter talent (Chapter 3).If your BAB is +16 or higher, you can deflect even boulders and siege missiles. You cannot throw these missiles back unless your Strength allows it and you normally have the ability to throw such large missiles.
Source: This feat also subsumes the Armed Deflection and Exceptional Deflection featsSRD. It supersedes the duelist’s Deflect Arrows prestige class feature.

sections.heading: Deft Blow [Finesse]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: BAB +1, Weapon Finesse.
Benefit: When using a slashing or piercing weapon in one hand to which Weapon Finesse applies (or a claw attack or crossbow), attacks with that weapon ignore up to 5 points of your opponent’s armor bonus to AC (if any). For every 4 points of your base attack bonus, increase the amount of armor bonus you can ignore by 1 (maximum 10 points at BAB +20).
Special: Unlike the Unstoppable Strike feat (q.v.), which resolves a melee attack as a touch attack, this feat can be used in conjunction with a full attack.
Source: This feat supersedes the Deft Strike featCAd. It subsumes the Free Hand Fighter’s timely tipAPG, being both more flexible (applying to armor and shield) and more efficient (not requiring a move action).

sections.heading: Far Shot [Ranged]
sections.text:
You are more accurate at longer ranges.
Benefit: You only suffer a –1 penalty per full range increment between you and your target when using a ranged weapon (not including rays and other ranged attack spells that do not have range increments).
Windage Shot [Strike]: If your BAB is +6 or higher, you can make a single ranged attack as a full round action that increases all range increments by half (for example, a bow with a normal range increment of 100 ft. would have a range increment of 150 ft.). At a BAB of +11, you can modify a ranged weapon and use in such a way that its range increments are increased by 50% even when you use it to make iterative attacks. If you make a windage shot, the weapon’s range increments are doubled instead (this supersedes the Archer’s legendary shotIH).At a BAB of +16, your range increments are always doubled. You also gain the Horizon Shot [Strike] ability: as a full-round action, you can make a single ranged attack, the range of which is limited only by how far you can see (regardless of the normal range of the weapon).
Normal: You suffer a –2 penalty per full range increment between you and your target.
Source: This feat subsumes the Distance ThrowerUC feat.

sections.heading: Favored Enemy [Skill]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Knowledge or other applicable skill (as applicable to creature type).
Benefit: Choose one creature type from the list shown under the Knowledge skill heading in Chapter 4; you must have at least 1 rank in the appropriate Knowledge or other applicable skill listed for that creature type in the table. You gain that class of creature as a favored enemy (as the Ranger lore), with a +1 bonus to attacks and relevant skills, and +2 to damage.
Your favored enemy bonus increases by an additional +1 (+2 to damage) for every 5 ranks in that skill past the 1st, to a maximum of +4 (+8 to damage) at 16 ranks.

sections.heading: Flanking Shot [Ranged]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1, Precise Shot, Point-Blank Shot.
Benefit: Whenever two of your allies are in melee with an enemy and at least one ally is providing an Aid Another bonus to the other’s attacks (i.e., is flanking it; see Chapter 7), you automatically gain a like circumstance bonus to ranged attacks made from within your point-blank range against that enemy.
In addition, when armed with a loaded ranged weapon, you can spend immediate actions to aid allies in combat (Aid Another) as long as they are within your point-blank range; they need not be within your reach.
If your BAB is +6 or higher, you can also receive Aid Another circumstance bonuses from allies to your ranged attack rolls against any targets, as long as the aiding allies are within your point-blank range. If your BAB is +11 or higher, you can use these abilities at any range.If your BAB is +16 or higher, you automatically gain a circumstance bonus to ranged attacks, as if by Aid Another, equal to twice the number of allies threatening the target (even if they are not spending immediate actions to aid one another or you).
Normal: You can flank only in melee.
Source: This feat was inspired by the Distant Advantage feat, from the 4th edition Players Handbook II. It also subsumes the Enfilading Fire featUC.

sections.heading: Grapple, Improved [Maneuver]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Martial Weapon Proficiency (unarmed attacks) or proficiency with natural attacks.
Benefit: You receive a +2 competence bonus on checks made to grapple a foe. This bonus increases by an additional +1 per 4 points of your base attack bonus. You gain a like bonus to your CMD against attempts to grapple or pin you. You do not provoke an attack of opportunity when you fail to grapple an opponent.
Grab: If your BAB is +6 or higher, you can start a grapple as a free action on a successful unarmed or natural attack. A successful hold does not deal any extra damage unless you also have the Vital Strike feat (see Synergy, below).Maintain Grapple: Also at BAB +6, once you have grappled a creature, you can maintain the grapple as a partial action. You suffer no penalty on attack rolls and can make attacks of opportunity while grappling, and you retain your Dexterity bonus to AC when pinning an opponent or when grappled. As a full attack you can make iterative grapple checks to move, pin, and/or damage a grappled opponent, as if you were making iterative attacks.Inescapable Grasp: If your BAB is +11 or higher, creatures you attempt to grapple or are grappling gain no benefit from freedom of movement or other magical bonuses to Escape Artist and/or on checks to escape a grapple. This is similar to the Tetori monk’s class feature of the same nameUC.Grappling Mastery: If your BAB is +16 or higher, you can apply multiple [Strike] effects to a grappled creature (see Synergy, below).
Synergy:
You can apply the effects of any [Strike] feat (q.v.) you possess when maintaining a damaging grapple or pin as a standard action (rather than attempting iterative damaging attempts using the maintain grapple function). Applying the Vital Strike feat with this effect allows you to add 1½ times your Strength bonus to the Vital Strike damage; this duplicates the Constrict abilityPB, and supersedes the Earth’s Embrace featCW.. Applying different other [strike] effects allows duplication of a number of feats and class features: Anchoring Blow or Ghost Strike—Tetori monk’s inescapable grasp abilityUC; Wolfsbane Strike—Tetori monk’s form lock abilityUC; etc.If you have the Two-Weapon Fighting feat and have a light weapon in one hand, you can perform damaging grapples and light weapon attacks in tandem with each other, as per two-weapon fighting. In conjunction with the Improved Trip feat (q.v.), this supersedes the Bear Fang featCW.
If you have a number of ranks in Escape Artist greater than or equal to a grappling opponent’s base attack bonus, you receive the following benefits:
When maintaining a grapple against an opponent, you are treated as entangled rather than grappled. Attempts to grapple you automatically provoke attacks of opportunity from you, even if this is not normally the case. If you deal damage with this attack, the enemy fails to start the grapple unless it also has the Improved Grapple feat. If the enemy has the feat, you may add the damage you deal as a circumstance bonus on your opposed check to resist being grappled. This does not give you extra attacks of opportunity when you would be denied one for being surprised, helpless, or in a similar situation. If your BAB is +6 or greater, you can make this attack of opportunity even if the attacker has concealment or total concealment; at BAB +11, even if you are flat-footed; and at BAB +16, even if your attacker has exceptional reach. This supersedes the Close-Quarters Fighting featCW and also the Tetori Monk’s counter-grappleUC. Note that if the attack of opportunity is used for a trip attempt, this function also supersedes the Under and OverAPG and the Felling EscapeUC feats.
Normal: You provoke an attack of opportunity when you fail to achieve a grapple. Maintaining a grapple, or grappling to move, pin, or damage an opponent, is a standard action.

sections.heading: Hammer FistRoF [Unarmed]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Str 13+, Martial Weapon Proficiency (unarmed).
Benefit: You are able to treat your unarmed attack as a two-handed weapon, gaining the more advantageous Strength bonus to damage and improved Power Attack damage. You can apply feats such as Backswing and Overhand Chop to your two-handed unarmed attacks.
When using an unarmed attack in this way, you cannot also treat it as a one-handed or light weapon for any purpose.

sections.heading: Hammer the GapUC
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Str 13, base attack bonus +6, Martial proficiency with a melee weapon (or proficiency with a natural attack), Vital Strike.
Benefit: If you hit the same enemy more than once in a single round with a single melee or natural weapon, you can apply your Vital Strike damage that round as well, even if the activating conditions are not otherwise met (i.e., this is similar to the Two-Weapon Strike feat (q.v.), but with a single weapon). Apply the additional damage only once, even if you hit more than twice
Synergy:
If you also have the Two-Weapon Strike feat, if you hit more than once with both weapons, apply your Vital Strike damage twice. This is a specific exception to the general rule against Vital Strike stacking with itself. This emulates the girallon windmill flesh rip maneuverToB. (A 16th level fighter hitting more than once with both weapons would deal an additional 12d6 + 1½ Str bonus damage). If you have the Mountain Hammer class feature, the doubling of Vital Strike damage occurs only once (maximum 18d6 + 1½ Str bonus damage).When this feat is activated while wielding a single weapon, you can apply the effects of one other [strike] you know in addition to the Vital Strike.
Source: This feat also supersedes the Jabbing Style featACG and the Flay Foe, Pulverize Foe, and Skewer Foe featsCoR.

sections.heading: Impaling Attack [Maneuver, Piercing]
sections.text:
You can catch your opponents on your weapon and hold them in place.
Prerequisites: Str 13, base attack bonus +6, Improved Grapple.
Benefit: Whenever you damage an opponent with a piercing weapon, you can immediately make a grapple check; success means the opponent is impaled on your weapon and you both gain the grappled condition. While the opponent is impaled, as an attack action you may make a grapple check on your turn to deal damage; you can do this even if your weapon cannot normally be used in a grapple. While you impale your opponent with your weapon, you cannot otherwise use it to attack, and you must hold on to it.
If your BAB is +11 or higher, while your opponent is impaled in this way, each time it starts its turn, it automatically takes normal damage from the weapon. As an immediate action, you can pull your weapon out of your opponent. Your opponent can also spend a move action to attempt a counter grapple check to pull your weapon out. When the weapon comes out, your opponent takes damage as if starting its turn impaled. If your BAB is +16 or higher, you can let go of your weapon, and the impaled opponent still must spend a standard action to remove the weapon. Until the opponent pulls the weapon out, its movement speed in all modes is halved.
Synergy:
If you have the Bleeding Strike feat, the effects of that feat apply when you withdraw your weapon from an impaled opponent.If you also have the Slowing Strike feat, the reduction in movement from that feat applies whenever an opponent is impaled (even if you are not still holding the weapon, if your BAB is +11 or higher; the victim is immobile while you hold the weapon, is slowed to 5 ft. once you let go, and moves at half speed once the weapon is removed).
Normal: You can only attack unarmed, or with a natural weapon or light weapon, against opponents you are grappling.
Source: This feat subsumes the Hamatula AttackPC, Hamatula GraspPC, Impaling CriticalUC, and (with synergy) Improved Impaling CriticalUC feats.

sections.heading: Manyshot [Ranged]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: BAB +1, Sleight of Hand 1 rank.
Benefit: When making a full attack with a ranged weapon, you can attack one additional time that round with no additional reload time (if applicable). All of your attack rolls take a –2 penalty when using this function.
If your BAB is +6 or higher and you have at least 6 ranks in Sleight of Hand, once per round you can fire two projectiles in place of a single ranged attack. Resolve them as two separate attacks, each with a -2 penalty. [Strike] effects, if applicable, apply only once. If your BAB is +11 or higher and you have at least 11 ranks in Sleight of Hand, you can make two additional attacks (one primary, one iterative) as part of a full attack.If your BAB is at least +16 and you have at least 16 ranks in Sleight of Hand, in lieu of your regular attacks, you can make a single ranged attack at each target within range, to a maximum number of targets equal to half your base attack bonus (normal reload times obviously do not apply in this case). Each attack uses your primary attack bonus, and each enemy may only be targeted by a single attack.
Source: This feat now subsumes the Rapid Shot and Manyshot featsCRB, and also the Greater Manyshot, Storm of Throws, and Swarm of Arrow featsSRD.
