Armored TrapIH

You constantly prepare counterattacks against opponents, timing your attacks to connect just as your armor baffles theirs.

Prerequisites: Heavy armor proficiency.

Benefit: When wearing armor and using a held attack (Chapter 7) against an opponent attacking you in melee, you gain a circumstance bonus to your attack equal to your armor training bonus (if any), and a circumstance bonus to damage equal to the AC bonus you receive from the armor (maximum +1 per point of your base attack bonus).

Block ArrowHB

You can block incoming arrows with your shield.

Prerequisite: Dex 13, Martial shield proficiency.

Benefit: To use this feat, you must be actively using a shield (not merely an animated shield or a shield spell). When you would normally be hit with a ranged weapon, you can spend an immediate action to deflect it so that you take no damage from it. You must be aware of the attack. Unusually massive ranged weapons, such as boulders hurled by giants and siege weapon attacks, can't be deflected.

Synergy:

  • If you also have the Shield Cover feat, you can parry ranged touch spells and attacks (such as rays) as if they were weapon attacks.
  • If you have the Armor Training fighter talent, this feat is superseded by the more general Shield Parry feat (q.v.).

Source: This feat also supersedes the Missile Shield and Ray Shield featsAPG.

Sacrificial Shield

Prerequisite: Martial shield proficiency.

Benefit: When you are struck in combat while using a shield, you can spend an immediate action to apply the damage to your shield. Subtract your shield's hardness and hit points (Chapter 6) from the damage of the attack; you take only the remainder (if any).

If the shield takes enough damage to destroy it, it's destroyed. Otherwise, it gains the broken condition, even if the damage was not enough to give it the broken condition under other circumstances.

Synergy: If you also have the Shared Shield feat, you can use this ability to protect an adjacent ally.

Source: This feat emulates the 2nd tier Guardian ability of the same nameMA.

Shield Bash, Improved

You can protect yourself with your shield, even if you use it to attack.

Prerequisites: Exotic Shield Proficiency, Two-Weapon Fighting.

Benefit: When you perform a shield bash, you may still apply the shield’s shield bonus to your AC.

  • If your BAB is at least +6, when shield bashing with a magic shield, your shield’s enhancement bonus to AC can be applied as an enhancement bonus to attacks and damage as well. The maximum enhancement bonus that can be applied in this manner is equal to +1 per 4 points of your base attack bonus.
  • If your BAB is at least +11, your shield bash deals damage as if your shield were one size larger (1d4 for a light shield, 1d6 for a heavy shield; or 1d6 for a light spiked shield, 1d8 for a heavy spiked shield). This does not stack with the bashing shield property.
  • If your BAB is at least +16, when fighting with a shield, you can make normal weapon attacks (with the two-weapon fighting penalty) but hold your shield bashes (Chapter 7 – held actions). Any time before your next turn, when you are attacked by an opponent, you can spend an immediate action to make one of the held shield bashes against that opponent; if this bash damages the target, the attack that triggered it misses. This simulates the Crusader’s shield counter maneuverToB.

SpecialAA: You can also force your shield into the mouth of a creature to prevent it from using bite attacks or other mouth-based abilities. Make a grapple check against a creature at least two sizes larger than your size category. If you succeed, you wedge your shield into its mouth. At any time you may release your shield, which means you both lose the grappled condition and return to your own squares, though your shield remains in its mouth. The creature may remove the shield by destroying it (or leaving it with the broken condition), forcing the shield out of its mouth with a grapple check against your CMB, or swallowing it (if it has the swallow whole ability) as if the shield were a creature.

While the shield is in place, the monster cannot use its mouth to make attacks (such as a bite or a giant frog’s sticky tongue) against anything but the shield and cannot speak clearly enough to cast spells or use items requiring speech. If it uses a breath weapon, its range is half normal and any damage dealt must first get through the shield, with any remaining damage affecting the area normally.

Synergy: If you also have the Improved Bull Rush feat, any opponents hit by your shield bash are also hit with a free bull rush attack, substituting your attack roll for the combat maneuver check. This bull rush does not provoke an attack of opportunity. Opponents who cannot move back due to a wall or other surface are knocked prone after moving the maximum possible distance. You may choose to move with your target if you are able to take a 5-foot step or to spend an action to move this turn. This supersedes the Shield Slam feat from the core rules.

Normal: Without this feat, a character that performs a shield bash loses the shield’s shield bonus to AC until his next turn. Magic shields do not apply their enhancement bonus to shield bashes.

Shield Cover

Prerequisite: Martial Shield Proficiency.

Benefit: When actively using a light, heavy, or tower shield (not a buckler, animated shield, or shield spell), your shield bonus (and any enhancement bonus it possessed) apply to your touch AC.

  • If your BAB is at least +6, you retain your shield bonuses while flat-footed. In addition, you may apply your shield bonus to Reflex saves (in the latter case, the shield’s enhancement bonus does not stack with resistance bonuses to Reflex saves, if any).
  • If your BAB is at least +11, your shield bonus applies to your CMD as well.
  • If your BAB is at least +16, when using a shield you are immune to effects that normally auto-confirm critical hits against you (Cf. Improved Critical).

Normal: Shield bonuses do not apply to flat-footed or touch AC, nor to CMD or reflex saves.

Source: This feat subsumes the Parrying ShieldLoM, Shield WardPHII, Shield SpecializationAPG feats, and the Knight of the Realm’s knightly defenseRRE.

Shield Parry

Prerequisites: Martial Shield Proficiency, Armor Training, base attack bonus +6.

Benefit: When actively using a shield (not an animated shield or a shield spell) you can use it to attempt one parry per round (Chapter 7) as an immediate action against an incoming attack. Penalties for Two-Weapon Fighting apply normally, but bonuses for Armor Training also apply.

Synergy:

  • If you also have the Shield Cover feat (q.v.), you can parry ranged touch spells and attacks as if they were weapon attacks. If your BAB is at least +11 and you use a magical shield to successfully parry an incoming ranged touch spell or attack (including a ray), you can redirect the effect at any target within the attack’s remaining range, including the original caster. Use the original spell’s attack roll, save DC, etc.
  • If you also have the Blind-Fight feat, you master the art of using the reflective surface of your shield to locate foes that you dare not look at directlyAA. On your turn, you may choose to forfeit your shield’s AC bonus for 1 round to improve your defenses against one creature using a gaze attack (if you also have the Improved Shield Bash feat, you can use this trick without losing the AC bonus). Your chance to avoid having to make a saving throw against that creature’s gaze attack increases to 100%, and the creature does not gain concealment against you. For every 5 ranks in Perception you have, you may simultaneously use this ability against one additional creature with a gaze attack.

Source: This feat replaces the Improved Shield Specialization and Reflective Shield featsCBEM.

Shield Proficiency, Martial

Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1, Simple Shield Proficiency.

Benefit: You gain Martial proficiency with all shields (Chapter 6).

Special: Barbarians, clerics, fighters, and paladins automatically have Martial Shield Proficiency as a bonus feat. They need not select it.

Shield Proficiency, Simple

You are trained in how to properly use shields.

Benefit: Simple proficiency with all shields.

Normal: When you are using a shield with which you are not proficient, you take the shield’s armor check penalty on attack rolls and on all Strength- and Dexterity-related skill checks.

Special: Bards, druids, incarnates, and rogues automatically have Simple Shield Proficiency as a bonus feat. They need not select it.

Shield Proficiency, Exotic

Prerequisites: Simple Shield Proficiency.

Benefit: Select one shield. You gain Exotic proficiency with that shield (Chapter 6).

Combat Feats, Weapon-and Style-Specific

The feats presented here are specific to certain weapons and/or combat styles, including dueling (finesse weapons), two-weapon fighting, and unarmed combat. Descriptors such as [Unarmed] and [Ranged] are provided for ease of reference; as with general combat feats, all feats in this section have the [Combat] descriptor, in addition to any others listed.

AxefightingCBEM [Axe, Slashing]

Prerequisite: Dex 13, base attack bonus +1, Weapon Specialization (any axe).

Benefit: Whenever you drop a foe (i.e., reduce him below 0 hp) with a qualifying axe, you gain a +2 morale bonus to attacks and damage with your weapon for 1 round, plus 1 round per 5 points of your base attack bonus above +1 (e.g., 4 rounds total at BAB +16).

Backswing [Two-Handed]

Prerequisites: Str 13, base attack bonus +6, Overhand Chop.

Benefit: When using the full-attack action with a two-handed melee weapon, primary bite attack, etc., add double your Strength bonus to damage, rather than 1½ times your Strength bonus.

Normal: You normally add 1½ times your Strength modifier to damage rolls with a two-handed weapon.

Source: This feat supersedes the variant class feature of the same nameAPG, the Exotic Weapon Master’s “uncanny blow” prestige class featureCW, and the Master Samurai’s “blades of death” prestige class featureS&F.

Bull Rush, Improved [Maneuver]

“If Igli manages to put on the brakes, I’ll hit him with a low tackle and knock him in. Then we all play water polo.” ―Robert A. Heinlein, Glory Road (1963)

You are skilled at blocking your foes and pushing them around the battlefield.

Prerequisites: Str 13, Power Attack.

Benefit: You receive a +2 competence bonus on checks made to bull rush, check, drag, or reposition a foe. This bonus increases by an additional +1 per 4 points of your base attack bonus. You gain a like bonus to your CMD for defending against these maneuvers as well. You do not provoke attacks of opportunity when failing to bull rush, check, drag, or reposition an opponent.

You gain the following improvements as you gain in combat experience:

  • Bull Rush Strike [Strike]: If your BAB is +6 or higher, you can make a single melee attack as a standard action; if it hits, you also gain a free bull rush attempt against that opponent. At the end of this movement, the target also falls prone if a second check on your part beats his CMD. This supersedes the Bull Rush Strike and Pushing Assault featsAPG. Combining the bull rush strike with Greater Overrun (see below) allows the duplication of the Driving Attack featPHII.
  • Greater Bull Rush: If your BAB is +11 or higher, whenever you bull rush or reposition an opponent in place of an attack (rather than in addition to an attack), the target’s movement provokes attacks of opportunity from all of your allies (but not you). This subsumes the Greater Bull Rush featCRB.
  • Knock Back: If your BAB is +16 or higher, whenever you deal weapon damage (in hit points) greater than a melee opponent’s CMD in a single blow in melee (not including energy or spell damage), you immediately gain a special bull rush attack against that opponent as a free action. If successful, the target is pushed back 10 feet; you do not move with it unless you choose to take a 5-ft. step into the space it was formerly in. This subsumes the Knock Back featRS, CBEM.

Synergy: You can combine a bull rush with other feats in a variety of ways:

  • If you have medium or heavy armor proficiency, respectively, you gain a +1 armor bonus to bull rush attempts when wearing medium armor, or a +2 armor bonus when wearing heavy armor.
  • If you have Exotic shield proficiency, you gain a +1 shield bonus to bull rush attempts when using a light shield, +2 with a heavy shield, and +3 with a tower shield.
  • If you have the Improved Trip feat and your BAB is +6 or higher, you can attempt to overbear an opponent by making a trip attempt as an immediate action at the end of a bull rush.
  • If you have the Improved Weapon Maneuvers feat and your BAB is +11 or higher, on a successful bull rush you slam into an opponent hard enough to make him drop whatever he’s holding (make a disarm check as a free action as the initial part of a bull rush attempt).
  • If you have the Power Attack feat and your BAB is +6 or higher (or your Strength is 25+), a successful bull rush strike (see above) throws the victim an additional 5 feet. This supersedes the Awesome Blow featPB, the Great ThrowOA and Ki ThrowAPG feats, and the various Swordsage mighty throw strikesToB (the latter particularly if combined with Vital Strike; see below).
  • If you have the Vital Strike feat, bull rushing a target back into a solid surface (such as a wall), rather than dealing your unarmed damage, instead inflicts Vital Strike damage plus 1½ times your Strength modifier. This supersedes part of the fighter’s “dungeon crasher” alternate class featureDS.
  • If you have the Whirlwind Strike feat and your BAB is +6 or higher, as a full-round action you can attempt to push back (bull rush) all foes within your reach. This supersedes the Wild SwingCBEM.

Normal: Failed combat maneuvers provoke attacks of opportunity. Creatures moved by combat maneuvers do not provoke attacks of opportunity.

Catch Off-Guard

“I’ll carry my weapons right through the check-point.”

“Oh, yes, I’d forgotten about that for a moment. ‘Naked/kill’ and all that. Stab a man with a drinking straw. What a nuisance that’s been...”

―Trevanian, Shibumi (1979)

Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.

Benefit: You do not suffer any penalties for using improvised ranged or melee weapons. Unarmed opponents are flat-footed to any attacks you make with an improvised melee weapon. You also receive a +1 competence bonus on attack rolls made with thrown splash weapons.

  • If your BAB is +6 or above and you have Exotic proficiency in unarmed attacks, increase the amount of damage you deal with improvised weapons by one step (for example, 1d4 becomes 1d6) to a maximum of 1d8 (2d6 if the improvised weapon is two-handed).
  • If your BAB is at least +11, your critical threat range with improved weapons is 19–20.
  • If your BAB is at least +16, when you confirm a critical hit with an improvised weapon, you can choose to increase the critical multiplier to x3, but the weapon itself also takes full critical damage from the attack (subject to hardness), and is therefore likely to be destroyed.

Synergy: If you have at least Martial proficiency with a light or heavy shield, you can use it as a throwing weapon with a range increment of 10 feet, dealing damage as from a shield bash. This supersedes the Shield Champion’s throw shield abilityACG.

Normal: You take a –4 penalty on attack rolls made with an improvised weapon.

Source: This feat also subsumes the Throw Anything and Improvised Weapon Mastery feats, and the “always armed” 1st tier Champion abilityMA.

Cloaked DuelistAotD [Finesse, Maneuver, Skill]

You use the very cloak on your back against an enemy, befuddling their attacks.

Prerequisites: Combat Expertise, Improved Weapon Maneuvers, Weapon Finesse; Sleight of Hand 1 rank.

Benefit: When fighting with a cloak on and at least one hand empty, you may as a free action sweep your cloak into your hand to aid you in a fight, treating it as a buckler. You may instead perform Bind maneuvers with your cloak.

  • If your BAB is at least +6 and you have at least 6 ranks in Sleight of Hand, you can parry with your cloak as well. If you fight defensively (Chapter 7) the cloak grants you a 20% miss chance from partial concealment, as if by a blur spell (this miss chance does not stack with other concealment-based miss chances, as from the Wind Stance feat).
  • If your BAB is at least +11 and you have at least 11 ranks in Sleight of Hand, when you use total defense (Chapter 7), your cloak grants you a 50% miss chance from concealment (as if by a displacement spell).
  • If your BAB is at least +16 and you have at least 16 ranks in Sleight of Hand, the miss chance is 50% when fighting defensively, and you are treated as if invisible when using total defense.

Synergy:

  • If you also have the Improved Grapple feat, you can use your cloak to entangle an opponent on a successful grapple check. The foe can get free by using a full-round action to escape or by destroying the cape (a typical cape has hardness 1 and 3 hit points). You can use this feat with items similar in shape and weight to a cape, such as a curtain. This subsumes the Dueling Cape featACG.
  • If you also have the Two-Weapon Fighting feat, treat your cloak as a light weapon for purposes of making off-hand binds or parries with it.

Clustered Attacks

“I'd have so much lead in his body they'd need a crane to get him off the ground.”

―Andrew H. Vachss, Hard Candy (1995)

You take a moment to carefully aim your blows or shots, causing them all to strike nearly the same spot.

Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +6, Weapon Specialization. You can substitute Precise Shot for Weapon Specialization, but in that case this feat applies only to ranged attacks.

Benefit: When you use a full attack action to make multiple weapon attacks (of the type for which you meet the prerequisite) against the same opponent, total the damage from all hits before applying that opponent’s damage reduction.

Massive damage applies if the total damage you deal with this feat is equal to or exceeds half the opponent’s full normal hit points (minimum 50 points of damage).

Source: This is the Clustered ShotsUC feat, expanded for use in melee as well.

Critical, Improved [Critical]

Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1, Martial weapon proficiency.

Benefit: Choose one weapon type (e.g., longsword) with which you have at least Martial proficiency. You receive a +4 circumstance bonus on attack rolls made to confirm critical hits with that weapon.

  • If your BAB is +6 or higher, your threat range with the selected weapon is doubled.
  • If your BAB is +11 or higher, all critical threats with the selected weapon are automatically confirmed.
  • If your BAB is +16 or higher, whenever you score a critical hit with the selected weapon, the critical damage multiplier increases by 1.

Synergy: If you have at least one [Strike] feat (q.v.), you can apply the effects of that strike to any confirmed critical hit, even if none of the normal conditions were met. This has the normal effects unless otherwise noted in that feat description. You still cannot add more than one [strike] effect to a given attack unless you also have the Striking Mastery fighter talent (q.v.).

The effects of this feat do not stack with keen edge, a keen weapon, or any other effect that increases the weapon’s critical threat range, except in the case of the Versatile Unarmed Combat feat (q.v.) and the fighter’s. versatile weapon use ability (Chapter 3).

Source: This feat subsumes the feat of the same name and also the Critical Focus featCRB; the BAB +16 function subsumes the Weapon Master’s Deadly CriticalAPG and the Master Thrower prestige class’s Deadeye Shot thrown weapon trickCW.

Crushing BlowPHII [Bludgeoning]

Your bludgeoning attacks are powerful enough to damage even heavily armored foes.

Prerequisites: Weapon Specialization with a bludgeoning weapon, base attack bonus +1.

Benefit: If you miss with a bludgeoning weapon by a margin less than your opponent’s armor and/or shield bonus (if any), you batter the foe for half normal damage.

  • If your BAB is +6 or higher, you also ignore up to 4 points of armor bonus.
  • If your BAB is +11 or higher, you ignore up to 8 points of your opponent’s armor bonus. Also, when you use a full attack action while fighting with any bludgeoning weapon, each attack that connects beats down your foe's defenses, granting a cumulative +2 circumstance bonus on attack rolls until the end of your current turn.
  • If your BAB is +16 or higher, you ignore up to 12 points of your opponent’s armor bonus.

Source: This feat also subsumes the Foe Hammer expanded mastery (4) effectIH, and the Macefighter featCBEM.

Deadly Aim [Ranged]

You can make exceptionally deadly ranged attacks by pinpointing a target’s weak spot, at the expense of making the attack less likely to succeed.

Prerequisites: Wis 13, base attack bonus +1.

Benefit: You can choose to take a -1 feat penalty to ranged attacks, but gain a circumstance bonus on damage. For every 4 points of your base attack bonus, increase the attack penalty by 1 (maximum -6 at BAB +20). The bonus to damage is dependent on the type of ranged weapon you are using:

  • For thrown weapons, the damage bonus is equal to the magnitude of the attack penalty.
  • For projectile weapons such as bows or slings, and for spells requiring ranged or ranged touch attack rolls (e.g., rays), you gain a +2 damage bonus per ­1 to attacks.
  • With crossbows and firearms (despite the latter being based on ray spells), you gain a +3 damage bonus per -1 to attacks.

Deflect Arrows [Finesse, Unarmed]

You can knock arrows and other projectiles off course, preventing them from hitting you.

Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1; Exotic Weapon Proficiency (unarmed attacks), Weapon Finesse, or Weapon Specialization.

Benefit: Depending on how you qualified for this feat, using it requires one of the following conditions: Exotic Proficiency (unarmed attacks)—one hand free (holding nothing); Weapon Finesse—holding manufactured finesse weapon; Weapon Specialization—wielding appropriate weapon.

Whenever you would normally be hit with a ranged weapon, you can spend an immediate action to deflect it so that you take no damage from it. You must be aware of the attack and not flat-footed. Unusually massive ranged weapons (such as boulders or ballista bolts), ranged touch attacks, and area-effect attacks can’t be deflected.

  • If your BAB is +6 or higher, you have at least 1 rank in Sleight of Hand, and have one hand free, instead of simply deflecting a thrown weapon, you can catch it and throw it back as an immediate action. This requires a Sleight of Hand check (DC = the results of the missile’s attack roll).
  • If your BAB is +11 or higher, you can deflect ranged spell attacks and spell-like abilities as if they were arrows, provided the attack in question specifically targets you and requires a ranged attack roll or ranged touch attack roll. You cannot “catch” magical attacks and return them, however, unless you also have the Parry Spells fighter talent (Chapter 3).
  • If your BAB is +16 or higher, you can deflect even boulders and siege missiles. You cannot throw these missiles back unless your Strength allows it and you normally have the ability to throw such large missiles.

Source: This feat also subsumes the Armed Deflection and Exceptional Deflection featsSRD. It supersedes the duelist’s Deflect Arrows prestige class feature.

Deft Blow [Finesse]

Prerequisite: BAB +1, Weapon Finesse.

Benefit: When using a slashing or piercing weapon in one hand to which Weapon Finesse applies (or a claw attack or crossbow), attacks with that weapon ignore up to 5 points of your opponent’s armor bonus to AC (if any). For every 4 points of your base attack bonus, increase the amount of armor bonus you can ignore by 1 (maximum 10 points at BAB +20).

Special: Unlike the Unstoppable Strike feat (q.v.), which resolves a melee attack as a touch attack, this feat can be used in conjunction with a full attack.

Source: This feat supersedes the Deft Strike featCAd. It subsumes the Free Hand Fighter’s timely tipAPG, being both more flexible (applying to armor and shield) and more efficient (not requiring a move action).

Far Shot [Ranged]

You are more accurate at longer ranges.

Benefit: You only suffer a –1 penalty per full range increment between you and your target when using a ranged weapon (not including rays and other ranged attack spells that do not have range increments).

  • Windage Shot [Strike]: If your BAB is +6 or higher, you can make a single ranged attack as a full round action that increases all range increments by half (for example, a bow with a normal range increment of 100 ft. would have a range increment of 150 ft.).
  • At a BAB of +11, you can modify a ranged weapon and use in such a way that its range increments are increased by 50% even when you use it to make iterative attacks. If you make a windage shot, the weapon’s range increments are doubled instead (this supersedes the Archer’s legendary shotIH).
  • At a BAB of +16, your range increments are always doubled. You also gain the Horizon Shot [Strike] ability: as a full-round action, you can make a single ranged attack, the range of which is limited only by how far you can see (regardless of the normal range of the weapon).

Normal: You suffer a –2 penalty per full range increment between you and your target.

Source: This feat subsumes the Distance ThrowerUC feat.

Favored Enemy [Skill]

Prerequisite: Knowledge or other applicable skill (as applicable to creature type).

Benefit: Choose one creature type from the list shown under the Knowledge skill heading in Chapter 4; you must have at least 1 rank in the appropriate Knowledge or other applicable skill listed for that creature type in the table. You gain that class of creature as a favored enemy (as the Ranger lore), with a +1 bonus to attacks and relevant skills, and +2 to damage.

Your favored enemy bonus increases by an additional +1 (+2 to damage) for every 5 ranks in that skill past the 1st, to a maximum of +4 (+8 to damage) at 16 ranks.

Flanking Shot [Ranged]

Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1, Precise Shot, Point-Blank Shot.

Benefit: Whenever two of your allies are in melee with an enemy and at least one ally is providing an Aid Another bonus to the other’s attacks (i.e., is flanking it; see Chapter 7), you automatically gain a like circumstance bonus to ranged attacks made from within your point-blank range against that enemy.

In addition, when armed with a loaded ranged weapon, you can spend immediate actions to aid allies in combat (Aid Another) as long as they are within your point-blank range; they need not be within your reach.

  • If your BAB is +6 or higher, you can also receive Aid Another circumstance bonuses from allies to your ranged attack rolls against any targets, as long as the aiding allies are within your point-blank range.
  • If your BAB is +11 or higher, you can use these abilities at any range.
  • If your BAB is +16 or higher, you automatically gain a circumstance bonus to ranged attacks, as if by Aid Another, equal to twice the number of allies threatening the target (even if they are not spending immediate actions to aid one another or you).

Normal: You can flank only in melee.

Source: This feat was inspired by the Distant Advantage feat, from the 4th edition Players Handbook II. It also subsumes the Enfilading Fire featUC.

Grapple, Improved [Maneuver]

Prerequisites: Martial Weapon Proficiency (unarmed attacks) or proficiency with natural attacks.

Benefit: You receive a +2 competence bonus on checks made to grapple a foe. This bonus increases by an additional +1 per 4 points of your base attack bonus. You gain a like bonus to your CMD against attempts to grapple or pin you. You do not provoke an attack of opportunity when you fail to grapple an opponent.

  • Grab: If your BAB is +6 or higher, you can start a grapple as a free action on a successful unarmed or natural attack. A successful hold does not deal any extra damage unless you also have the Vital Strike feat (see Synergy, below).
  • Maintain Grapple: Also at BAB +6, once you have grappled a creature, you can maintain the grapple as a partial action. You suffer no penalty on attack rolls and can make attacks of opportunity while grappling, and you retain your Dexterity bonus to AC when pinning an opponent or when grappled. As a full attack you can make iterative grapple checks to move, pin, and/or damage a grappled opponent, as if you were making iterative attacks.
  • Inescapable Grasp: If your BAB is +11 or higher, creatures you attempt to grapple or are grappling gain no benefit from freedom of movement or other magical bonuses to Escape Artist and/or on checks to escape a grapple. This is similar to the Tetori monk’s class feature of the same nameUC.
  • Grappling Mastery: If your BAB is +16 or higher, you can apply multiple [Strike] effects to a grappled creature (see Synergy, below).

Synergy:

  • You can apply the effects of any [Strike] feat (q.v.) you possess when maintaining a damaging grapple or pin as a standard action (rather than attempting iterative damaging attempts using the maintain grapple function). Applying the Vital Strike feat with this effect allows you to add 1½ times your Strength bonus to the Vital Strike damage; this duplicates the Constrict abilityPB, and supersedes the Earth’s Embrace featCW.. Applying different other [strike] effects allows duplication of a number of feats and class features: Anchoring Blow or Ghost Strike—Tetori monk’s inescapable grasp abilityUC; Wolfsbane Strike—Tetori monk’s form lock abilityUC; etc.
  • If you have the Two-Weapon Fighting feat and have a light weapon in one hand, you can perform damaging grapples and light weapon attacks in tandem with each other, as per two-weapon fighting. In conjunction with the Improved Trip feat (q.v.), this supersedes the Bear Fang featCW.

If you have a number of ranks in Escape Artist greater than or equal to a grappling opponent’s base attack bonus, you receive the following benefits:

  • When maintaining a grapple against an opponent, you are treated as entangled rather than grappled.
  • Attempts to grapple you automatically provoke attacks of opportunity from you, even if this is not normally the case. If you deal damage with this attack, the enemy fails to start the grapple unless it also has the Improved Grapple feat. If the enemy has the feat, you may add the damage you deal as a circumstance bonus on your opposed check to resist being grappled. This does not give you extra attacks of opportunity when you would be denied one for being surprised, helpless, or in a similar situation.
  • If your BAB is +6 or greater, you can make this attack of opportunity even if the attacker has concealment or total concealment; at BAB +11, even if you are flat-footed; and at BAB +16, even if your attacker has exceptional reach. This supersedes the Close-Quarters Fighting featCW and also the Tetori Monk’s counter-grappleUC. Note that if the attack of opportunity is used for a trip attempt, this function also supersedes the Under and OverAPG and the Felling EscapeUC feats.

Normal: You provoke an attack of opportunity when you fail to achieve a grapple. Maintaining a grapple, or grappling to move, pin, or damage an opponent, is a standard action.

Hammer FistRoF [Unarmed]

Prerequisites: Str 13+, Martial Weapon Proficiency (unarmed).

Benefit: You are able to treat your unarmed attack as a two-handed weapon, gaining the more advantageous Strength bonus to damage and improved Power Attack damage. You can apply feats such as Backswing and Overhand Chop to your two-handed unarmed attacks.

When using an unarmed attack in this way, you cannot also treat it as a one-handed or light weapon for any purpose.

Hammer the GapUC

Prerequisites: Str 13, base attack bonus +6, Martial proficiency with a melee weapon (or proficiency with a natural attack), Vital Strike.

Benefit: If you hit the same enemy more than once in a single round with a single melee or natural weapon, you can apply your Vital Strike damage that round as well, even if the activating conditions are not otherwise met (i.e., this is similar to the Two-Weapon Strike feat (q.v.), but with a single weapon). Apply the additional damage only once, even if you hit more than twice

Synergy:

  • If you also have the Two-Weapon Strike feat, if you hit more than once with both weapons, apply your Vital Strike damage twice. This is a specific exception to the general rule against Vital Strike stacking with itself. This emulates the girallon windmill flesh rip maneuverToB. (A 16th level fighter hitting more than once with both weapons would deal an additional 12d6 + 1½ Str bonus damage). If you have the Mountain Hammer class feature, the doubling of Vital Strike damage occurs only once (maximum 18d6 + 1½ Str bonus damage).
  • When this feat is activated while wielding a single weapon, you can apply the effects of one other [strike] you know in addition to the Vital Strike.

Source: This feat also supersedes the Jabbing Style featACG and the Flay Foe, Pulverize Foe, and Skewer Foe featsCoR.

Impaling Attack [Maneuver, Piercing]

You can catch your opponents on your weapon and hold them in place.

Prerequisites: Str 13, base attack bonus +6, Improved Grapple.

Benefit: Whenever you damage an opponent with a piercing weapon, you can immediately make a grapple check; success means the opponent is impaled on your weapon and you both gain the grappled condition. While the opponent is impaled, as an attack action you may make a grapple check on your turn to deal damage; you can do this even if your weapon cannot normally be used in a grapple. While you impale your opponent with your weapon, you cannot otherwise use it to attack, and you must hold on to it.

  • If your BAB is +11 or higher, while your opponent is impaled in this way, each time it starts its turn, it automatically takes normal damage from the weapon. As an immediate action, you can pull your weapon out of your opponent. Your opponent can also spend a move action to attempt a counter grapple check to pull your weapon out. When the weapon comes out, your opponent takes damage as if starting its turn impaled.
  • If your BAB is +16 or higher, you can let go of your weapon, and the impaled opponent still must spend a standard action to remove the weapon. Until the opponent pulls the weapon out, its movement speed in all modes is halved.

Synergy:

  • If you have the Bleeding Strike feat, the effects of that feat apply when you withdraw your weapon from an impaled opponent.
  • If you also have the Slowing Strike feat, the reduction in movement from that feat applies whenever an opponent is impaled (even if you are not still holding the weapon, if your BAB is +11 or higher; the victim is immobile while you hold the weapon, is slowed to 5 ft. once you let go, and moves at half speed once the weapon is removed).

Normal: You can only attack unarmed, or with a natural weapon or light weapon, against opponents you are grappling.

Source: This feat subsumes the Hamatula AttackPC, Hamatula GraspPC, Impaling CriticalUC, and (with synergy) Improved Impaling CriticalUC feats.

Manyshot [Ranged]

Prerequisites: BAB +1, Sleight of Hand 1 rank.

Benefit: When making a full attack with a ranged weapon, you can attack one additional time that round with no additional reload time (if applicable). All of your attack rolls take a –2 penalty when using this function.

  • If your BAB is +6 or higher and you have at least 6 ranks in Sleight of Hand, once per round you can fire two projectiles in place of a single ranged attack. Resolve them as two separate attacks, each with a -2 penalty. [Strike] effects, if applicable, apply only once.
  • If your BAB is +11 or higher and you have at least 11 ranks in Sleight of Hand, you can make two additional attacks (one primary, one iterative) as part of a full attack.
  • If your BAB is at least +16 and you have at least 16 ranks in Sleight of Hand, in lieu of your regular attacks, you can make a single ranged attack at each target within range, to a maximum number of targets equal to half your base attack bonus (normal reload times obviously do not apply in this case). Each attack uses your primary attack bonus, and each enemy may only be targeted by a single attack.

Source: This feat now subsumes the Rapid Shot and Manyshot featsCRB, and also the Greater Manyshot, Storm of Throws, and Swarm of Arrow featsSRD. It also subsumes the Arcane Archer’s hail of arrowsSRD, the Fighter-Archer’s volleyAPG, and the Master Thrower’s power throw and two with one blow prestige class featuresCW.

Medusa’s Wrath [Unarmed]

You can take advantage of your opponent’s condition, delivering multiple blows.

Prerequisites: BAB 11+, Martial Weapon Proficiency (unarmed attacks), Staggering Strike.

Benefit: When making a full unarmed attack against a dazed, flat-footed, paralyzed, staggered, stunned, or unconscious foe, you can make two additional unarmed attacks at your highest attack bonus.

Melee EvasionPHII [Melee]

Prerequisites: Combat Expertise, Dodge.

Benefit: While fighting defensively, you can spend an immediate action to gain improved defense against one attack. Instead of applying the AC bonus from the Combat Expertise feat, instead treat your normal and touch AC as if they were 1d20 + your BAB + your Dodge bonus.

Misdirection Tactics [Skill]

Prerequisites: Combat Expertise, Bluff 6 ranks.

Benefit: While you are using the total defense action, if a melee attack would still hit your AC, you can attempt a Bluff check with a DC equal to the foe’s attack roll as an immediate action. If you succeed at the check, you negate the attack (treat it as a miss). If the attack still hits, you cannot use this feat against the same opponent during that encounter.

  • If you have at least 11 ranks in Bluff, when you would successfully negate an attack using this feat, you can instead redirect the attack to a different target of your choice within the foe’s reach.
  • If you have at least 16 ranks in Bluff, you can make an attack of opportunity (despite the usual prohibition on making attacks of opportunity while using total defense) against any opponent whose attack you negate or redirect using this feat.

Source: This feat subsumes the feat of the same name, and also the Misdirection Redirection and Misdirection Attack featsUI.

Overrun, Improved [Maneuver]

You are skilled at ramming past opponents and running them down.

Prerequisites: Str 13, Power Attack.

Benefit: You receive a +2 competence bonus on checks made to overrun a foe. This bonus increases by an additional +1 per 4 points of your base attack bonus. You gain a like bonus to your CMD for defending against overruns, against the Counter Charge maneuver (Chapter 7), and as a competence bonus to saving throws against trample attacks. You do not provoke attacks of opportunity when you fail to overrun an opponent.

You gain the following improvements as your skill at combat improves:

  • Improved Overrun: If your BAB is +6 or higher, you can overrun as an attack action, rather than as a standard action (you can make iterative overrun attempts in this manner even if you do not normally receive iterative attacks, as in the case of creatures using natural weapons). If you fail to overrun an opponent, the target can’t knock you prone; your movement merely stops in the last legal space you occupy. This subsumes the boulder roll maneuverToB and also the Phalanx Fighter’s “stand firm” variant class featureAPG.
  • Greater Overrun: If your BAB is +11 or higher, whenever you overrun opponents, they provoke attacks of opportunity if they attempt to avoid you or are knocked prone by your overrun. This subsumes the Greater Overrun feat from the core rules.
  • Charge Through: If your BAB is +16 or higher, you can charge through allies’ spaces without impediment. When making a charge, you can attempt to overrun creatures in the straight-line path of the charge as free actions. If you successfully overrun a creature in the way, you can complete the charge. If the overrun is unsuccessful, the charge ends in the space directly in front of that creature. This supersedes the feat of the same nameAPG and the Juggernaut Charge featCBEM.

Synergy: You can combine charging and overrunning with other feats in a variety of ways:

  • If you have medium or heavy armor proficiency, respectively, you gain a +1 armor bonus to overrun attempts when wearing medium armor, or a +2 armor bonus to overrun attempts when wearing heavy armor.
  • If you have Exotic shield proficiency, you gain a +1 shield bonus to overrun attempts when using a light shield, +2 with a heavy shield, and +3 with a tower shield.
  • If you have the Skirmish and Vital Strike feats, you can use them to deal Vital Strike damage to creatures you successfully overrun, in addition to the creature attacked at the end of the charge (see Skirmish, q.v.). This simulates the trample special attack from the Bestiary.
  • If your BAB is +11 or higher and you have the Improved Weapon Maneuvers feat, on a successful overrun you slam into an opponent hard enough to make him drop whatever he’s holding (in practice, you can make a disarm check as a free action as the initial part of a bull rush or overrun attempt).

Normal: Failed combat maneuvers provoke attacks of opportunity. Creatures moved by combat maneuvers do not provoke attacks of opportunity. Creatures that avoid your overrun or are knocked prone do not provoke an attack of opportunity.

Parry, Open-Handed [Unarmed]

Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +6, Combat Expertise, Dodge, Exotic Weapon Proficiency (unarmed attacks).

Benefit: Once per round when you have at least one hand free and are either fighting defensively or using the total defense action, as an immediate action you can attempt to parry (see Chapter 7) one melee attack that would normally hit you. You must be aware of the attack and not flat-footed. An attack so deflected deals no damage to you.

Synergy: If you also have the Combat Reflexes feat, you can make an immediate counterattack (an attack of opportunity, costing an additional immediate action) against any opponent whose attack you parry in this manner.

Source: This feat supersedes the Crane Wing and Crane Riposte featsUC.

Phalanx Fighter [Polearm]

Prerequisite: Weapon Specialization (polearm or spear); Martial shield proficiency.

Benefit: You can use any qualifying polearm or spear of your size as a one-handed weapon when using a qualifying shield with your other arm.

Synergy:

  • If you also have Exotic proficiency with the designated weapon and with light shields, you can use the weapon two-handed and still gain the benefits of a light shield; this emulates the Shield and Pike Style featDr338.
  • When using this feat with a tower shield, you can brace a light or heavy crossbow against the shield and fire one-handed without the usual penalty. You still cannot reload one-handed, however, without using the Sleight of Hand skill.

Source: This feat supersedes the “phalanx fighter” variant class featureAPG.

Point-Blank Shot [Ranged, Skill]

You are especially accurate when making ranged attacks against close targets.

Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1, Perception 1 rank.

Benefit: You get a +1 circumstance bonus to attack and damage rolls with ranged weapons at close range (up to 25 ft. + 5 ft./2 points of your BAB).

  • If you have at least 6 ranks in Perception and your BAB is at least +6, the range increases to Medium (100 ft. + 10 ft. per point of BAB) and the bonus increases to +2.
  • If you have at least 11 ranks in Perception and your BAB is at least +11, the range increases to Long (400 ft. + 40 ft. per point of BAB) and the bonus increases to +3.
  • If you have at least 16 ranks in Perception and your BAB is at least +16, the range increases to Extreme (1,000 ft. + 100 ft. per point of BAB) and the bonus increases to +4.

Readied Shot: If you use a held or readied action to fire a ranged weapon at point-blank range at any foe who charges you, each +1 damage bonus from this feat becomes +1d6 precision damage instead (maximum +4d6 at BAB +16).

Synergy:

  • The range at which you can deal precision (e.g., sneak attack) damage is equal your point-blank range.
  • When using the Improved Two-Weapon Fighting feat while wielding a melee weapon and a crossbow or firearm, your attacks with the crossbow or firearm provoke no attacks of opportunity from foes that you threaten with your melee weapon. This supersedes the Sword and Pistol featUC.

Source: This feat incorporates the Hyborian Ranger class feature of the same name, from Hyboria.Xoth.net, and has also been combined with the Ready Shot featHB. It supersedes the Sniper’s “deadly range” variant class featureAPG.

Power ThrowCAd [Ranged]

Prerequisites: Strength 13+.

Benefit: You can combine a charge with a hurled weapon attack, moving towards the target and taking a -2 penalty to AC in exchange for a +2 bonus to attack.

Whenever you use two hands to throw a one-handed or two-handed weapon (not a light weapon), you gain a bonus on damage rolls equal to 1½ times your Strength bonus. Using two hands to throw any weapon requires only a partial action for you.

  • If your BAB is at least +6 and your Dexterity is 13 or greater, you can also apply half your Dexterity bonus (in addition to your Strength bonus) to damage with weapons thrown with one hand.
  • If your BAB is +11 or higher, you can apply your full Dexterity bonus (if any), as well as your Strength bonus, to damage with weapons thrown with one hand.
  • If your BAB is +16 or higher, you can apply both your Strength bonus and your Dexterity bonus (if any) to attacks with weapons thrown with one hand.

Synergy:

  • If you have the Power Attack feat, you can use that feat in conjunction with thrown weapons.
  • You cannot use the Deadly Aim feat in conjunction with this feat.

Normal: Power Attack can be applied only to attacks with melee weapons. You add your Strength bonus on thrown weapon damage, regardless of available hands. Throwing a two-handed weapon is a full-round action.

Source: This feat also subsumes the Brutal ThrowCad, Charging HurlerUC, Two-Handed ThrowerUC and Hurling ChargeMH feats. It also supersedes the Hulking Hurler’s ranged power attack prestige class featureCW.

Precise Shot [Ranged]

You are adept at firing ranged attacks into melee.

Benefit: You can shoot or throw ranged weapons at an opponent engaged in melee without taking the standard –4 penalty on your attack roll.

  • If your BAB is +6 or higher, when you use ranged weapons against a non-adjacent grappling or pinned opponent, you run no risk of hitting the wrong target.
  • If your BAB is +11 or higher, your ranged attacks also ignore the AC bonus granted to targets by anything less than total cover, and the miss chance granted to targets by anything less than total concealment. If you miss due to total concealment, you can immediately reroll once to see if you actually hit. You gain no more than one reroll per attempt.
  • At a BAB of +16, as a full-round action you can take a single shot against an opponent with full cover, ignoring the cover by ricocheting the shot.

Normal: Firing into a melee has a –4 circumstance penalty; if you miss a grappled target by a margin of 4 or less on the roll, the shot targets the grappling creature instead.

Synergy:

  • You can deal precision damage with ranged attacks against targets with partial concealment if you have this feat and your base attack bonus is at least +6. You can deal ranged precision damage against targets with total concealment if your effective BAB is +11 or higher.
  • If you have at least 11 ranks in Stealth as a class skill, opponents struck by your ranged attacks (and observers) do not automatically know what square your attack came from, and must attempt to find you normally.

Source: The advanced usages of this feat supersede the Improved Precise Shot feat and the Archer’s legendary shot class featureIH, and the Elven Accuracy featAPG.

Ranged Maneuvers [Maneuver, Ranged]

Prerequisites: Exotic Proficiency and Weapon Specialization in the appropriate ranged weapon; Improved Combat Maneuvers (any) and/or Cleave.

Benefit: You can perform combat maneuvers with qualifying ranged weapons, and can also apply the Cleave feat to ranged attacks. You must have the Improved Combat Maneuvers or other feat to be applied, and must meet all of its prerequisites.

Source: This feat supersedes Ranged Mastery featCBEM and also the “meteor shot” and “trick shot” variant class featuresAPG. The ranged feint function replaces the Master Thrower’s “sneaky shot” prestige class thrown weapon trickCW, and also can simulate the Archer’s “unerring shot” token abilityIH.

Ranged ThreatDr350 [Ranged]

Prerequisites: Point-Blank Shot.

Benefit: When armed with a ranged weapon that is ready for use, you threaten every square within 5 ft., plus 5 ft. per 4 points of your base attack bonus. If a target in this area takes an action that provokes an attack of opportunity, you may make a ranged attack of opportunity at your highest bonus. You do not provoke attacks of opportunity when making a ranged attack of opportunity.

  • If your BAB is +6 or higher, you can make a covering shot as a standard action. Covering Shot [Strike]: When you miss with a ranged attack made as a standard action, you can pin down the target of that missed attack as a free action. The pinned-down target is treated as if it were entangled for 1 round. This supersedes the Gunslinger’s “covering shot” deedUC.
  • If your BAB is +11 or greater, you can choose for the target of your covering shot to be flat-footed for 1 round, rather than entangled. You cannot choose to purposely miss a target to gain this effect. This supersedes the Gunslinger’s “startling shot” deedUC.
  • If your BAB is +16 or higher, you do not provoke attacks of opportunity when using a ranged weapon from a threatened square. This supersedes the Combat Archery featSRD.

Synergy:

  • If you also have the Combat Reflexes feat, you can choose to forego threatening nearby squares and instead lay down threatening fire. As a standard action, designate a straight line of squares to which you have a clear line of fire. All of the squares must lie within the same range increment of you. Opponents moving through those squares provoke ranged attacks of opportunity from you; this effect ends when you move. This supersedes the Suppressive Fire featSwA.
  • If you have the Manyshot feat, when making a full-attack action with a ranged weapon, you may choose to make a melee attack against an adjacent opponent with a drawn arrow or bolt (or with the butt of the weapon itself) rather than firing it. If the attack hits—whether or not it does damage—your target is pushed back 5 feet away from you. You can then fire the weapon normally, at the original target, or at another target within range. This melee attack replaces the extra attack from Manyshot, and all of your attack rolls for the round (the melee attack and the ranged attacks) take a –2 penalty. If your initial attack leaves you with no enemies threatening you, you can make the subsequent ranged attack or attacks without provoking attacks of opportunity. This subsumes the Stabbing Shot featAPG.

Normal: While wielding a ranged weapon, you threaten no squares and can make no attacks of opportunity with that weapon. Ranged attacks provoke attacks of opportunity from threatening opponents.

Source: This feat also supersedes the Order of the Bow Initiate “close combat shot” prestige class feature, the Exotic Weapon Master’s “close quarters ranged shot” and the Master Thrower’s “defensive toss” stuntsCW; the Close-Quarter Fire featCBEM; the Close-Quarters Thrower feat and the Snap Shot feat chainUC; and the Point Blank Master feat, the Archer’s and Crossbowman’s “safe shot” variant class feature, and the Zen Archer’s “reflexive shot” variant class featureAPG.

Reflexive Shot [Ranged]

You are so practiced with ranged weapons that you fire them from pure reflex and “muscle memory” as much as from careful aim.

Benefit: When using a projectile weapon and/or making a ranged touch attack, you may use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Wisdom modifier on attack rolls. Alternatively, when using a thrown weapon, you may use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier.

  • If your BAB is +6 or greater, you can apply half your Dexterity modifier on damage rolls. When using a crossbow or firearm, you can instead apply your full Dexterity bonus to damage.
  • If your BAB is +11 or higher, you can apply your full Dexterity modifier as a bonus to damage with ranged weapons. When using a crossbow or firearm, you can apply your full Dexterity bonus and your Wisdom bonus (if any) to damage.
  • If your BAB is +16 or higher, you can apply both your Wisdom bonus (if any) and your Dexterity modifier to attacks with ranged weapons.

Source: This feat supersedes the Crossbowman’s Deadshot chain of variant class featuresAPG, and also the Gunslinger’s gun training class featureUC.

Scything Blow [Two-Handed]

Prerequisite: Str 13, base attack bonus +1, Power Attack.

Benefit: When using a slashing or piercing weapon in both hands (or a primary bite or gore attack), your melee attacks ignore up to 5 points of your opponent’s armor and/or shield bonus. For every 4 points of your base attack bonus, increase the amount of armor/shield bonus you can ignore by 1 (maximum 10 points at BAB +20).

Source: This feat is similar to the Deft Strike featCAd (q.v.), but applies to two-handed weapons.

Shared Precision [Ranged]

Your skill at archery inspires your allies to follow your mark.

Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +6, Deadly Aim, Precise Shot.

Benefit: When you hit a creature with a ranged attack, allies within 10 feet of you gain the benefit of the Precise Shot feat against that target until the start of your next turn. Your allies must remain within 10 feet of you, and must be able both to see and hear you to gain this benefit.

  • If your BAB is +11 or higher, you and any allies within 10 feet no longer provide cover against each other’s ranged attacks unless they wish to. Allies who cannot move or otherwise take action still provide cover, as do flat-footed allies. You and your allies must be able to see or hear each other to use this ability.
  • If your BAB is +16 or higher, allies within 10 feet of you also gain the effects of the Deadly Aim feat against the designated target, even if they lack the prerequisites.

Source: This feat supersedes the Divine HunterUC shared precision, aura of care, and hunter’s blessing variant class features.

Shield of BladesUI

Your wild attacks allow you to block your foes’ counterattacks.

Prerequisite: Power Attack.

Benefit: When you make melee attacks with the Power Attack feat, you gain a shield bonus to AC equal to your penalty to attack rolls from Power Attack. This lasts until the beginning of your next turn.

Shorten GripDr331 [Polearm]

Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +6, Martial Weapon Proficiency (any polearm).

Benefit: When wielding a polearm with which you have at least Martial proficiency and that has reach, you may treat the weapon as if it did not have reach. The weapon is unwieldy in this fashion and you take a –2 circumstance penalty on attack rolls when attacking an enemy you normally could not.

If your base attack bonus is at least +6, the penalty for attacking adjacent targets is eliminated.

Normal: Reach weapons cannot be used against adjacent foes.

Source: This feat also supersedes the Short Haft featPHII.

SpearfighterCBEM [Piercing, Spear]

You keep foes at bay with jabs from your spear.

Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1, Weapon Specialization (spear, long spear, or short spear).

Benefit: When using a qualifying spear, any foe that charges you provokes an attack of opportunity.

  • If your BAB is at least +6, attacks of opportunity against a charging opponent are always made as if you had braced your weapon to receive the charge (Chapter 6).
  • If your BAB is at least +11, any foe within reach who makes a full attack against you, or who moves towards you and then attacks you during the same turn, also provokes an attack of opportunity with your spear.
  • If your BAB is at least +16, attacks of opportunity granted by this feat are always made as if you had braced your weapon to receive the charge, even if the target is not charging.

Trip, Improved [Maneuver]

Prerequisites: Dex 13, Martial Weapon Proficiency (unarmed attacks or tripping weapon, or primary natural attack).

Benefit: You do not provoke an attack of opportunity if you fail to trip or unbalance an opponent. In addition, you receive a +2 competence bonus on checks made to trip or unbalance a foe. This bonus increases by an additional +1 per 4 points of your base attack bonus. You gain a like bonus to CMD when defending against these maneuvers. Your ability to trip people improves as you gain in combat experience:

  • Drag DownUC: If your BAB is +6 or higher, whenever an opponent successfully trips you, you can attempt to trip that opponent as an immediate action.
  • Maneuver Training: If your BAB is +6 or higher, you gain the effects of the Maneuvering Strike feat (trip or unbalance only), even if you do not possess that feat. This supersedes the tripping function of the Punishing Kick featAPG.
  • Greater Trip/Greater Unbalance: If your BAB is +11 or higher, whenever you successfully trip an opponent, that opponent provokes an attack of opportunity from you. Whenever you unbalance an opponent as a combat maneuver, he or she is treated as flat-footed and cannot make attacks of opportunity.
  • KnockdownSRD: If your BAB is +16 or higher, whenever you deal damage (in hit points) greater than a melee opponent’s CMD in a single blow, you immediately gain a trip attack against that opponent as a free action. However, you do not gain an attack of opportunity (see below) when tripping an opponent through the use of this function.

Synergy:

  • If your BAB is +6 or higher and you also have the Improved Bull Rush and Vital Strike feats, opponents you trip are slammed against the floor, taking Vital Strike damage plus 1½ times your Strength modifier (assuming a hard surface).

Normal: You provoke an attack of opportunity when attempting a trip or unbalance combat maneuver that fails. Creatures that are knocked prone do not provoke attacks of opportunity; off-balance creatures lose their Dex bonus to AC, but are not otherwise flat-footed.

Two-Weapon Defense

So saying, he gripped his staff and threw himself upon his guard. Then the Tinker spat upon his hands and, grasping his staff, came straight at the other. He struck two or three blows, but soon found that he had met his match, for Robin warded and parried all of them. ―Howard Pyle,

The Merry Adventures of Robin Hood (1883)

Prerequisites: Two-Weapon Fighting.

Benefit: When wielding a double weapon or two weapons (not including natural weapons or unarmed strikes), you gain a +1 shield bonus to your AC.

  • This bonus increases by an additional +1 per 5 points of your base attack bonus thereafter (i.e., +2 at BAB +6, +3 at BAB +11, and +4 at BAB +16). Also, when you are fighting defensively, using the total defense action, or using the Combat Expertise feat, this shield bonus increases by an additional +1.
  • If your BAB is +16 or higher, apply the enhancement bonus of your off-hand weapon also applies to the shield bonus to AC from this feat as well.

Synergy: If you have the Weapon Finesse feat and are fighting with a finesse weapon in one hand and a light weapon in the other, you may choose to fight defensively with your off-hand weapon, while fighting normally with your primary weapon. The penalty for fighting defensively applies to all attacks with your off-hand weapon only, and you still gain the bonus to AC. You may not use total defense in this manner. This use of the feat supersedes (does not stack with) the normal AC bonus provided by the feat.

Source: This feat supersedes the Two-Weapon Warrior’s “defensive flurry” variant class featureAPG and the Mythic Two-Weapon Defense featMA. The synergy use also supersedes the Dagger Defense featAotD.

Two-Weapon Fighting

You can fight with a weapon in each hand, making one attack each round with the second weapon in addition to your primary hand attacks.

Prerequisite: Dex 13.

Benefit: Your penalties on attack rolls for fighting with two weapons are reduced. You make attacks with your primary weapon at -2, and with your secondary weapon at -5 (or -2, if it is a light or natural weapon).

Creatures with multiple natural attack forms, and that cannot make iterative attacks with a primary natural attack, do not suffer the -2 penalty to primary natural attacks.

Synergy:

  • A monk can use the Two-Weapon Fighting feat to perform a so-called “flurry of blows” in conjunction with any combination of weapons, unarmed attacks, and/or combat maneuvers (assuming the weapon(s) are in hand and the monk has at least Simple proficiency with them). For example, a 1st level monk can attack with two unarmed attacks, or with each of a pair of sickles, or twice with a single sickle, or with a sickle and an unarmed attack, etc., as long as the total number of attacks matches that gained with the Two-Weapon Fighting feat. Flurrying with a two-handed weapon limits your damage bonus from Strength and Power Attack to that of a one-handed weapon, however. You can flurry with ranged weapons, subject to the normal reload times (for projectiles) and Sleight of Hand requirements (for thrown weapons).
  • Monsters with more than two arms (as from the obah-blessedDu136 or arachnoidUD template) can instead gain “Multiweapon Fighting;” designating one weapon as the primary weapon, and rest all being treated as off-hand weapons.

Special: In addition to attacking with two separate weapons (or a double weapon), Two-Weapon Fighting can also be used in conjunction with any of the following:

  • A single polearm held in both hands (taking the off-hand attacks with the haft; treat as a staff). Secondary attacks gain ½ your Strength modifier for damage, as normal for two-weapon fighting, and gain damage bonuses from Power Attack as if using a light weapon.
  • A finesse weapon used in one hand (attacking with the pommel as a knuckle-duster for your off-hand attacks; treat as a light club).
  • Alternatively, you can activate two wands (one in each hand) as a standard action, applying the attack penalty as a penalty to Spellcraft checks made to activate them (and applying the attack penalties normally, if the wand emits a ray or something similar).

Normal: As a partial action, a character can attempt to simultaneously attack with both a primary weapon and a secondary weapon (off-hand weapon, bite (if available), etc. When fighting in this way you suffer a −6 penalty with your primary attack and a –9 penalty to the secondary attack. If your secondary attack is with a light or natural weapon, those penalties are reduced by 4 each (-2/-5). In either case, the wielder can apply only half his/her Strength bonus (or Dex bonus, for Weapon Finesse and BAB +6) to the secondary attack’s damage.

Activating a wand is a standard action.

Source: This feat now subsumes the MultiattackCRB, Haft StrikeDr331, Double Wand WielderCA feats, and the Swashbuckler’s pommel swipe deedACG.

Two-Weapon Fighting, Improved

You are skilled at fighting with two weapons.

Prerequisites: Dex 13, base attack bonus +6, Two-Weapon Fighting.

Benefit: Add your full Strength bonus to damage rolls made with your off-hand weapon (or Dexterity bonus, if using a finesse or light weapon in conjunction with the Weapon Finesse feat). In addition, you can make iterative attacks with your off-hand weapon.

If you are using multiple forms of natural attacks, iterative attacks do not apply, but all of your natural attacks are made at the full attack bonus (-0) and use your full Str and/or Dex modifier for damage.

Normal: Without this feat, you can only get a single extra attack with an off-hand weapon, and add only half your Strength bonus to damage with an off-hand weapon.

Source: This feat subsumes the Greater Two-Weapon Fighting feat, and incorporates the Double Slice feat as well. Because it can be used with thrown weapons, it subsumes the Master Thrower’s “doubletoss” prestige class featureCW.

Prerequisite: Str 13, Two-Weapon Fighting.

Benefit: When wielding a one-handed weapon in your off-hand, you take penalties for fighting with two weapons as if you were wielding a light weapon in your off-hand.

Two-Weapon Strike

Prerequisites: Two-Weapon Fighting or two claw attacks.

Benefit: If you hit an opponent with both your primary attack and your off-hand attack (or both claw attacks) during the same round, you can apply the effects of one [Strike] feat you possess, even if the normal activating conditions have not been met.

Synergy:

  • When used in conjunction with the Vital Strike feat in melee, you also add 1½ times your Strength bonus to the Vital Strike damage. This supersedes the Two-Weapon Rend and Rending Claws featsAPG, and the Twin Thunders featUC. You cannot also apply the Mountain Hammer ability, however (see Advanced Fighter Talents).
  • If you have the Versatile Unarmed Combat feat (q.v.) and have two hands free, your unarmed attacks count as claw attacks for purposes of qualifying for this feat and activating it. This supersedes the Boar Style featUC (in conjunction with the Daunting Strike feat (q.v.), it also subsumes the Boar Ferocity featUC; in conjunction with the Bleeding Strike feat (q.v.), it subsumes the Boar ShredUC and Greater Rending FuryUC feats as well).
  • When used in conjunction with Maneuvering Strike feat, this feat subsumes the Two-Weapon Warrior’s “deft doublestrike” class featureAPG (disarm or sunder), and the Crescent Moon (disarm), Hammer’s Edge (trip), and High Sword Low Axe (trip) featsCW.
  • In conjunction with the Sickening Strike feat, it supersedes the Three Mountains featCW.
  • In conjunction with the Staggering Strike feat, this feat supersedes the Twin Thunders Master featUC.

Two-Weapon Versatility

Prerequisites: Improved Two-Weapon Fighting, Two-Weapon Fighting.

Benefit: When fighting with two different weapons, any weapon-specific benefits from feats or talents (such as Weapon Specialization or the Improved Critical feat) that you receive with one weapon automatically apply to the other as well. If you already receive one or more of these benefits with the other weapon, the effects overlap, rather than stack.

  • If your BAB is +11 or greater, magical properties possessed by one weapon apply to both (whether innate properties of the item itself or imbued by a spell, class feature, etc.). If there is an overlap, use the best of each category; raw enhancement bonuses do not stack.

Source: This feat supersedes the Tempest prestige class feature of the same nameCW and the Dual Enhancement featACG. It can also be used to simulate the Two-Weapon Warrior’s “twin blades” variant class featureAPG.

Unarmed Combat, VersatilePHII [Unarmed]

You employ a variety of unarmed fighting styles, allowing you to alter the type of damage your attacks deal.

Prerequisite: Exotic Weapon Proficiency (unarmed attacks).

Benefit: As a swift action, you can opt for your unarmed strikes to deal your choice of bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. Once you make this choice, your unarmed strikes continue to deal the chosen damage type until you use another swift action to change it.

  • If your BAB is +6 or higher, you can change the damage type as a free action. In addition, for each consecutive round that you change the type of damage selected from the previous round, the threat range of your unarmed attack increases by 1, to a maximum of 15-20/x2 after 4 rounds (2 rounds if you also have the Improved Critical feat).
  • If your BAB is +11 or higher, your unarmed attacks can deal two different types of damage simultaneously (e.g., bludgeoning and slashing).
  • If your BAB is +16 or higher, your unarmed attacks deal bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. For purposes of increasing the threat range (see above), the damage type is treated as if it were re-assigned each round.

Weapon Finesse [Finesse]

You are trained in using your agility in melee combat, as opposed to brute strength.

Benefit: With a light weapon, natural weapon, or weapon with the [finesse] property made for a creature of your size category, you may use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier on attack rolls and when calculating CMB. Additionally, you can substitute your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier when calculating any Strength-dependent DCs for [strike] feats (q.v.) and/or [strike] talents you possess.

If you carry a shield, its armor check penalty applies to your attack rolls.

  • If your BAB is +6 or greater, you can apply your Dexterity bonus instead of your Strength bonus on damage rolls as well as attack rolls. Any Strength penalty to damage still applies, however.
  • If your BAB is +11 or higher, you can apply your Strength modifier and/or your Dexterity modifier to damage (either or both, at your option), and can choose which modifier to apply to attacks and CMB.
  • If your BAB is +16 or higher, you can apply both your Strength bonus (if positive) and your Dexterity bonus to attacks, CMB, and damage.

Special: Other feats requiring this feat gain the [Finesse] descriptor.

Synergy: You cannot use this feat in conjunction with the Power Attack feat.

Source: This feat also subsumes the Agile ManeuversCRB, Fury’s FallPC, Shadow BladeToB feats, the Aldori Swordlord’s Deft Strike prestige class featurePOP, and the Mythic Weapon Finesse featMA.

You can apply finesse to weapons that do not normally allow it.

Prerequisites: Str 13, Dex 13, Martial Weapon Proficiency, Weapon Finesse.

Benefit: Choose a weapon group for which you have at least the Martial level of proficiency. You can use all weapons from that group in conjunction with the Weapon Finesse feat, even if this is not normally possible.

Weapon Maneuvers, Improved [Maneuver]

“Thy sword cannot stand against an oaken staff such as mine. I could snap it like a barley straw.”

―Howard Pyle,

The Merry Adventures of Robin Hood (1883)

Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.

Benefit: You receive a +2 competence bonus on checks made to bind, disarm, parry, or sunder a foe’s weapon. This bonus increases by an additional +1 per 4 points of your base attack bonus. You gain a like bonus to the DC for performing these combat maneuvers against you as well. When attacking an object, you ignore 1 point of the object’s hardness per +1 bonus granted by this feat.

You do not provoke an attack of opportunity when you attempt a bind, disarm, or sunder combat maneuver and fail.

If your BAB is +6 or greater, you gain the following additional abilities:

  • Blade Binder: Whenever you successfully bind an opponent’s weapon with yours, that opponent gains grappled and flat-footed conditions until he wrests his weapon free (by succeeding at a combat maneuver check as an attack action) or drops it (as a free action) on his turn. Dropping the weapon provokes an immediate attack of opportunity from you (the opponent is aware of this if he or she succeeds at a passive Knowledge (warfare) check; if this fails, a successful combat maneuver check against you as a free action also reveals this information). This function supersedes the Blade Binder featPC.
  • Disarm, Greater: Whenever you successfully disarm an opponent, the weapon lands a number feet away from its previous wielder equal to your disarm CMB check results, in a random direction. You can choose the direction by reducing the distance by 5 ft.; if you cause the weapon land within 15 ft., you specify the exact location (including into your off-hand, if desired).
  • Disarming Block: Whenever you successfully parry a weapon in melee (Chapter 7), you can make a disarm attempt against the weapon parried as an immediate action. This supersedes the Grappling Block featOA.
  • Blinding/Disarming/Sundering Strike (Strike): As a standard action, you can make a single melee attack. If it hits, you gain a bind, disarm, or sunder attempt (your choice) against that opponent as a free action. You can use this attack in conjunction with the Vital Strike feat (q.v.). This emulates the Warblade’s disarming strike maneuverToB and, if a sundering strike causes the broken condition (Chapter 7) in a weapon, the exorcism of steel strikeToB.
  • Sunder Object: When attacking an object or structure, you deal double damage.
  • Sundering Parry: If you successfully use a held action to parry an opponent’s attack, you can automatically attempt to sunder the weapon; this does not require an action. This emulates the Crushing Defense featDr301.

If your BAB is +11 or higher, you gain the following additional abilities:

  • Halbschwert: You can wield any weapon with which you have at least Martial proficiency against a foe grappling you, without the normal penalty. This simulates one function of the Weapon Supremacy featPHII.
  • Sunder, Greater: Whenever you sunder armor or shield and destroy it, any excess damage is applied to the wielder/wearer (no damage is transferred if you decide to leave the item with 1 hit point). If you sunder an opponent's armor or shield and destroy the item with a single hit, you instead deal an amount of damage to your opponent equal to the total amount of damage you dealt to destroy the armor or shield (this supersedes the Deadly Concussion featDr333.

If your BAB is +16 or higher, you gain the following additional ability:

  • Sunder, Aggressive: When you successfully sunder a weapon using your weapon, you cause broken pieces of the sundered weapon to strike its bearer. Immediately make an attack roll (as a free action) against the weapon's wielder (using only your base attack bonus and any masterwork or enhancement attack bonus the sundered weapon had). If this attack hits, the target takes damage as if he was struck by the weapon in its unsundered state. This option is from Sean K Reynolds’ web site.

Synergy: There are two major areas of synergy:

  • Come to Grips: If you have the Improved Grapple or Improved Trip feat, after a successful parry or bind with a Finesse weapon, you may immediately make a trip attempt or initiate a grapple as a free action that does not provoke an attack of opportunity. This option duplicates the Come to Grips featAotD. Historical Note: Wrestling was often used as a foundation for weapon training, and many sword instructors integrated swordplay with wrestling, especially in Germany and Italy.
  • Swashbuckler: If you have the Weapon Finesse feat, are wielding a light or one-handed weapon in one hand, and have nothing in your other hand, then the bonuses granted by this feat are doubled. (This allows a better simulation of the various swashbuckling movies with Douglas Fairbanks and Errol Flynn.)

Normal: Failed combat maneuvers provoke attacks of opportunity. Disarmed weapons and gear land at the feet of the disarmed creature. You cannot ignore item hardness when sundering, and excess sundering damage is wasted.

Source: This feat combines the Improved Disarm, Improved Sunder, Greater Disarm, and Greater Sunder feats from the core rules.

Combat Feats, Stances

Unless otherwise specified, a stance requires a move action to activate (Chapter 7). Once initiated, it lasts until you adopt another stance (as a swift action), or until you move (see below), after which time it can be re-adopted as a move action on your next turn. You cannot maintain a stance while dazed, helpless, staggered, stunned, or unconscious.

While in a stance, you cannot willingly move from your current position through any means (including normal movement, riding a mount, teleportation, or willingly allowing allies to carry you). If you enter a stance while on a moving vehicle you do not control (such as a wagon or ship), you can maintain the stance even if the vehicle moves. However, if you move under your own power as a result of an enemy’s successful use of the Bluff skill or an enchantment spell―or suffer any uncontrolled movement, as by a Bull Rush or telekinesis effect―your stance ends.

Unless noted otherwise in the description, it is not possible to gain the effects of more than one stance at a time unless you have the Stance Mastery feat (q.v.).

Special: All [stance] feats are also [combat] feats, although the [combat] descriptor is omitted in the titles.

  • If your BAB is at least +11, when you divert an enemy’s attack from an adjacent ally, that enemy provokes attacks of opportunity from all of your adjacent allies.

Because the bonus is a circumstance bonus, the effects of multiple successful critical hits stack.

  • If your BAB is +16 or higher, the opponent’s effective reach is reduced by 20 ft. (minimum 5 ft.) or by 15 ft. (minimum 0 ft.).
